decision.title: Cloud attach starts syncing in-process — the linkedHub boot-pin is lifted for the consented path only
decision.rationale:
Pressing Connect in the cloud panel used to do nothing observable: the attach lane stored the hub credential and wrote linkedHub into .design/config.json, but the sync runtime captures cfg.linkedHub once at boot and reloadConfig deliberately refuses to hot-swap it (a committed, repo-travelling config must never re-point the sync socket — DDR-149 fan-out review). The UI paid for that invariant with the sentence 'Linked to <X> — restart the studio server to start syncing': a task with no button behind it, naming a component that does not exist for a desktop user. Reported 2026-08-05 with a screenshot.

Decision: split the two paths the boot-pin was conflating.

1. A linkedHub arriving FROM DISK stays boot-pinned and refused — reloadConfig is unchanged. The threat model (a poisoned/attacker-authored config.json in a cloned repo silently re-pointing sync) is untouched.
2. A linkedHub the person JUST AUTHORIZED in trusted app chrome — exchanged against the configured cloud address, with the matching hub credential stored by this same process one line earlier — is adopted in memory and applied by a real stop()+start() cycle.

Mechanism: a new module apps/studio/sync/supervisor.ts (createSyncSupervisor) becomes the sole owner of the live SyncRuntime lifecycle; server.ts no longer holds the runtime directly and publishes the supervisor on ctx.syncControl. context.ts gains adoptLinkedHub(ctx, linkedHub) as the ONE way cfg.linkedHub may change on a running server; it takes the value BY VALUE from the attach lane and never re-reads .design/config.json, so the file-watcher's refused capability cannot return through a side door. cloud/endpoints.ts linkToWorkspace calls ctx.syncControl.restart(linkedHub) and returns a typed sync outcome {syncing, canvases, reason, detail}; the panel reports an outcome ('Syncing with X — N canvases') or the server's own refusal reason, never a restart instruction. Refusals that createSyncRuntime only logged (unlinked / no-credential / insecure-url / nothing-syncable / error) are re-derived by the supervisor so a dialog can say something true; the zero-syncable arm repeats the runtime's own _sync.json reason rather than inventing a second explanation that could drift.

Adjacent fix forced by the change: linkToWorkspace overwrote linkedHub wholesale, dropping a project-wide syncTsx:false opt-out (DDR-072/DDR-079). Harmless while nothing synced until a restart; a real disclosure now that Connect syncs immediately — so the restrictive direction (false only, never true) is carried across a re-link.

Alternatives rejected: (a) a 'Restart now' button — the desktop shell has no restart-sidecar command, and the honest answer to 'why doesn't it do it itself' is that it should; (b) making reloadConfig hot-swap linkedHub for everyone — that is exactly the capability DDR-149 refused, and the file is not where consent lives; (c) leaving the copy and only rewording it — the person would still be doing the product's job.

Verified live, not just in unit tests: a dev-server booted against a scratch project with a stubbed control plane + cell answered POST /_api/cloud/attach with {sync:{syncing:true,canvases:1}}, /_sync-status reported the live runtime immediately, a second Connect cleanly cycled it, and the config watcher emitted no 'not hot-reloadable' warning (the adopted value equals the written one). Tests: apps/studio/test/sync-supervisor.test.ts (incl. one end-to-end case through the real createSyncRuntime) + cloud-endpoints coverage of the outcome and the syncTsx carryover.

decision.title: smart-frames gemma tier runs on two interchangeable scout runtimes — mlx-vlm (preferred) or Ollama
decision.rationale: User feedback: the Gemma model install story was too complicated (mlx-vlm is a manual Python install, and a bare `pip install mlx-vlm` fails on PEP 668 externally-managed Pythons). Two changes: (1) the mlx-vlm install command shown in Settings is now a copy/paste one-liner that creates a Maude-managed venv (~/.maude/mlx-venv, XDG-aware) which resolveMlxPython probes automatically — the command is computed server-side from the same path the probe checks so they can never drift; the install stays USER-RUN per DDR-183. (2) Ollama is a new alternative scout runtime: `ollama pull gemma3:4b` (vision-capable tags only — gemma3:1b and gemma3n are text-only and excluded) unlocks the gemma tier with no Python at all. Ollama has no video input, so the scout ffmpeg-samples ≤16 evenly-spaced timestamped frames and sends them as images to /api/chat; coarser than mlx's native video path, acceptable because scout beats only ADD candidates — ffmpeg cuts stay the precise backbone (DDR-183). mlx-vlm is preferred when both are present (the benchmarked path). Settings card shows both copy/paste commands and re-probes every 10 s so it unlocks itself after the user runs one. Manifest gains a `scout: mlx|ollama` field. Env knobs: OLLAMA_HOST, MAUDE_OLLAMA_MODEL.

decision.title: Ollama scout endpoint is loopback-pinned — the footage pipeline stays egress-free
decision.rationale: Both security reviewers (defender + attacker pass, .ai/logs/security-reviews/gemma-ollama-scout-runtime*.md) independently flagged that an unvalidated $OLLAMA_HOST would silently upload the user's video frames to a remote/LAN host and turn the TTL-cached server probe (GET /_api/generate/keyframe-model → ollamaStatus) into a blind SSRF emitter — contradicting the DDR-183 posture that the footage pipeline is egress-free by design. Resolution, mirroring the DDR-185 curl-local precedent: ollamaHost() (both copies — generation/gemma-models.ts and bin/_smart-frames.mjs) accepts only literal loopback hosts (127.x.x.x, ::1, localhost; no DNS names — a resolvable name could point anywhere or rebind), returns null otherwise, and both fetches use redirect:'manual' plus content-length caps; the scout temp dir is mkdtempSync and model-authored beat labels are control-stripped + capped at 120 chars before entering the manifest. Consequence: a remote Ollama is deliberately NOT supported — supporting one would need an explicit consent surface, not an env var.

decision.title: Scout setup routes are server-probed capabilities, not hardcoded client copy — script over brew, link over button
decision.rationale: The Settings card hardcoded `brew install ollama` and a python3 venv one-liner, both dead ends on a machine without Homebrew or python3 (user-reported). Ownership of 'how do I install this' moves from the client to the server: gemma-models.ts now probes platform/arch/curl/brew/python3 and the ollama binary (TTL-cached, same DoS reasoning as the other probes) and exports ollamaSetupOptions()/mlxSetup(), returning an ORDERED list of routes that work on THIS machine; the client renders that list verbatim and owns no install copy. Three sub-decisions: (1) Ollama's official install.sh is the PRIMARY route ahead of brew on macOS and Linux — verified from the script source that Darwin is handled (fetches Ollama-darwin.zip into /Applications) and it needs only curl, so it works where brew doesn't; brew is offered only when brew exists. (2) The ollama.com download route renders as a COPYABLE LINK, never a button: DDR-054 gives the desktop shell no general URL opener (each opener is host-locked in Rust), so a button would silently no-op in the packaged .app — adding an ollama.com opener would widen that surface and need a Rust command + capabilities + build.rs. (3) installed-but-not-running is a distinct state carrying the opposite advice (`ollama serve`), and mlxSetup() returns a stated REASON instead of a command when the machine can't run it. Known gap left open: the whisper.cpp subtitles card has the identical brew-only hardcoding and would be the natural second consumer of this probe layer — Ollama cannot serve it (official docs: text/chat/embeddings/vision/tools/thinking/web-search, no audio or ASR capability), so only the setup UX unifies, never the runtime.

decision.title: Scout model downloads are runtime-aware — an Ollama box pulls through /api/pull, not a dead mlx button
decision.rationale: User feedback on the rendered card: it was a wall of seven options, the disabled button used its LABEL as the error message ('Needs mlx-vlm'), and — the real defect — the Download buttons only ever spoke for the mlx runtime, so a machine running Ollama saw dead buttons on models it could never use. decision.title: Canvas-lane Request rebuilds live in cell-config.mjs and must ride the original request as init source
decision.rationale: A Worker Request rebuilt as new Request(url, { ...request, headers }) copies NOTHING from the source request — method and body are prototype getters, invisible to object spread — so every canvas-origin write (annotation strokes, artboard layout, media) crossed the data plane as a bodyless GET. The studio answered writes from its GET branches with a 200 the client read as saved; changes crossed as cursors and died as documents THROUGH the v0.55.0 hub-door fix (canvas-origin-http-writes-at-capability-role), because the method never survived long enough to reach the door that fix repaired. Decision: (1) the two rebuild sites are extracted from worker.mjs into cell-config.mjs as exported pure functions canvasInnerRequest / stripCanvasOriginMarker — cell-config is the dependency-free module the node test suite can import (worker.mjs pulls @cloudflare/containers, unresolvable under plain node), so testability drives the ownership boundary; (2) the invariant is behavioral and pinned by canvas-request.test.mjs: a PUT crosses the rebuild as a PUT, body intact, and the canvas-origin marker is asserted by the Worker alone; (3) the two canvas-origin marker guards in canvas-origin.test.mjs moved from source-regex over worker.mjs to behavioral assertions against the same functions — a source regex pins an inline shape and cannot see a lossy rebuild, which is exactly how this bug shipped. Rule for future code: rebuild a Request only via new Request(url, request) / new Request(request) and mutate headers on the fresh copy; never spread a Request into an init object. Fixed in commit 7a59f9e4, deployed same day via wrangler deploy (Worker-only change — no image rebuild, no cell restart needed).

decision.title: Transcription gains an `auto` engine — DDR-164's no-silent-switch rule kept by making auto a SELECTED, self-declaring mode
decision.rationale: User asked for the subtitle engine to switch to ElevenLabs Scribe automatically when a key is present. DDR-164 (Task 2.6) had deliberately made the engine an EXPLICIT choice so Maude would never silently reach for a paid, off-machine engine — and that rationale is load-bearing, not bureaucratic: one ElevenLabs key covers audio GENERATION and Scribe ('one key for the whole stack'), so a key added for music/TTS would otherwise be enough to start uploading the user's audio and billing their account for transcription they never chose. Resolution keeps the rule instead of reversing it: `auto` joins whisper|elevenlabs|groq as a mode the user SELECTS, and it always declares its resolution — the Settings card renders 'Right now Auto uses <engine> — <reason>' plus an explicit 'audio is uploaded to that provider and billed to your account' when cloud, and the CLI prints 'auto → …' before transcribing. Precedence: elevenlabs (accuracy beats a local base model) > groq > local whisper; an UNRELATED provider key (e.g. Google for images) never moves audio off-machine, which is a test. Config-schema enum, prefs vocabulary and the CLI's KNOWN_PROVIDERS all gain `auto`; absent config still means whisper, so no existing install changes behavior without the user picking auto. Second half of the same change: the subtitle card now PROBES whisper.cpp (mirroring _transcribe.mjs's resolution exactly, including its refusal to probe a bare `main` — a prior security finding) and shows machine-viable setup routes in the two-step shape, since whisper.cpp ships prebuilt binaries for Linux/Windows but NOT macOS, making 'a cloud engine' the honest brew-less answer. Shared TTL-cached PATH/spawn probing extracted to generation/runtime-probe.ts, now used by both the scout and subtitle stacks. NOT unified: the RUNTIME — Ollama has no ASR capability (official docs: text/chat/embeddings/vision/tools/thinking/web-search), so subtitles can never move onto it.

decision.title: Studio route DNS-rebind guard is mode-aware: loopback Host locally, hub x-maude-role vouch in a cell
decision.rationale: The studio gated ~97 route handlers on isLoopbackHost(req.headers.get(host)) as a DNS-rebinding defence. In a cell that check can never pass — the hub proxy rewrites Host to the project public name (D4, upstreamHeaders) — so every browser-shell project write (Inspector CSS, artboard resize/style/kind, insert/delete/reorder, edit-attr/text) 403d with local request required, while annotations/comments worked only because their handlers carry no such guard. Decision: introduce one helper isTrustedRequestHost(req) in apps/studio/http.ts and route all 98 call sites through it. It returns true for a loopback Host (verbatim local behaviour) OR, when isWorkspaceMode(), when the request carries an injected x-maude-role header. That header is unforgeable proof of hub provenance because the proxy strips every inbound x-maude-* before injecting its own — the same WORKSPACE ? x-maude-role vouch the collab-WS upgrade in server.ts already trusts. Safe against secret leakage by construction: a cell PRUNES every secret-bearing route family from its table (pruneForWorkspace + the containment boot-assert), so the vouched path can only reach the project-editing surfaces that survive. Second, established invariant: a write-classified manifest entry must never be a GET-only handler — /_api/edit-scope was filed {safe:null,unsafe:edit} but is a GET-only read (Local/Shared badge), so the hub answered the shell GET 405 for every role. Fixed to {safe:read,unsafe:null} and pinned by a new source-scrape guard in studio-manifest.test.mjs that fails the build on any future inversion. This is the third distinct layer of the cloud editor write path repaired in one day, after canvas-lane-request-rebuild-preserves-method-and-body (worker method-drop) and the /auth/login role storage. Fix committed + validated (hub 474/474, studio 3528/0); reaches a live cell only via a cell-IMAGE rebuild, not wrangler deploy, because http.ts + the manifest run inside the container.

decision.title: sameOriginWrite compares host+port, not full origin — TLS terminates at the cell proxy
decision.rationale: The studio CSRF guard sameOriginWrite (apps/studio/http.ts, 78 write routes) compared the browser Origin header against new URL(req.url).origin — a full-origin equality including scheme. In a cell TLS terminates at the hub proxy: the browser sends Origin https://<host> but the studio serves plaintext and computes req.url as http://<host>, so the scheme differed and every legitimate shell write was refused with 403 cross-origin write rejected. This was the SECOND cell-incompatible guard on the shell write path, uncovered only after the loopback fix (decision:studio-route-guard-mode-aware-hub-vouch) let requests reach it; the two together are why the cloud Inspector could annotate/comment but not edit. Decision: compare host+port only (new URL(origin).host === new URL(req.url).host), the same host-only reasoning isOwnShellOrigin in studio-proxy.mjs already uses for the collab WS upgrade for the identical TLS-termination reason. Safe: scheme was never the CSRF discriminator (locally everything is http, and a real cross-site page has a different host), and the port still pins the origin. The change is unconditional (not workspace-gated) because host-only is strictly correct in both modes. sameOriginRead is untouched — it keys on Sec-Fetch-Site, already scheme-agnostic. Verified live on alligators: edit-css with no/http Origin reached the handler (422 element-not-found) before this change; this closes the https-Origin case a real browser sends. Committed 21a7b7a2.

decision.title: The fleet nav has exactly one door, and it is the dashboard
decision.rationale:
Cloud Phase 26 gated the operator surface twice on purpose: at the route (404 for anyone outside OPERATOR_ACCOUNT_IDS) and again at the shell, because a nav entry a customer can see but not open is an invitation to try, and the section's existence is itself information they have no reason to hold. appShell therefore renders the Fleet section only when passed isOperator: true.

What shipped left that flag with one caller. operator-pages.mjs set it; the other five appShell callers — dashboard.mjs, project-admin.mjs, people-page.mjs, checkout-pages.mjs, device-auth.mjs — did not, and none of them computed the predicate at all. The observable consequence: the Fleet nav appeared only once you were ALREADY inside /operator, so the surface had no way in except typing the URL. The allowlist was doing its job; nothing linked to what it unlocked.

DECIDED: the predicate is evaluated for exactly one customer-facing page. auth-routes.mjs (which has env in scope at the signed-in GET / branch) calls isOperator(env, account) and threads it into dashboardPage, which forwards it to the shell. The dashboard is where a signed-in person starts, so that is where the door belongs.

DECIDED AGAINST threading it into the remaining four. project-admin, people-page, checkout and device-auth stay on the isOperator = false default. Two reasons. A payment or device-pairing flow is not a place to grow navigation — the nav would be noise at the moment the page is asking for one specific thing. And every additional caller that computes the predicate is another site where the gate can be got wrong; one door is one place to audit. The default-false parameter is what keeps those four pages byte-identical rather than merely equivalent.

The shell gate itself is UNCHANGED, and so is the rule behind it — a customer still renders no /operator string and no Fleet heading anywhere, which operator-pages.test.mjs already asserted and dashboard.test.mjs now asserts again at the page level. What changed is only that the predicate is finally evaluated outside /operator.

Tested at two levels on purpose, because they catch different regressions. dashboard.test.mjs covers the render contract (flag on renders the door, default renders nothing, a customer holding a project renders nothing). auth-routes.test.mjs covers the wiring end to end through a real worker.fetch with a session cookie and the account id in OPERATOR_ACCOUNT_IDS — that one fails if a future edit drops the env threading, which the render-level test alone could not see.

decision.rationale: Divergent /flow:plan debate converged 3-0 swap-no (BUILDER, SHIPPER, BREAKER, each confidence 4). decision.title: Container write bridge synthesises fs:any in workspace mode — canvas-edit relies on an unreliable inotify recursive watch
decision.rationale: In a cell, source edits (Inspector CSS, artboard, insert/reorder) reached disk but never live-re-rendered for a peer browser — the peer sat on the pre-edit module until a manual reload, while annotations crossed live. Root cause (verified live: a 200 edit-css delivered nothing to a connected canvas-hmr socket): canvas-edit.ts writes every edit atomically via Bun.write(tmp)+rename into a designRoot subdir (25 sites) and emits NO bus event — it depends on fs-watch.ts (fs.watch(designRoot,{recursive:true})) to notice and fire fs:any, which drives the HMR broadcaster and the peer canvas-hmr socket. macOS FSEvents catches the rename; the Linux container inotify emulated recursive watch MISSES the atomic rename into a subdir, so fs:any never fires. Decision: add createContainerWriteBridge(ctx) in hmr-broadcast.ts, wired WORKSPACE-MODE-ONLY in ws.ts. decision.rationale:
# DDR-213: A cell syncs to itself, or to nothing

**Date:** 2026-08-06
**Status:** accepted
**Tags:** cloud/cell/collab/crdt/yjs/shared-doc/autocommit/extends-ddr-064/extends-ddr-209
**Supersedes:** —
**Extends:** [DDR-064](DDR-064-single-shared-collab-doc.md), [DDR-209](DDR-209-one-studio-three-shells-the-cell-serves-the-studio.md)
**Plan:** [`feature-desktop-cloud-live-pairing.md`](../../plans/feature-desktop-cloud-live-pairing.md)

## Context

Cloud Phase 27 put the real studio inside the cell, and a member opening
`<project>.cloud.maude.sh` now loads the byte-identical client the desktop
loads. What they do not get is the other person.

A cell holds **two disjoint `Y.Doc` worlds**:

| | who connects | where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the hub's Hocuspocus documents | the **desktop** (`linkedHub` → the cell) | hub process, SQLite-backed, durable |
| the studio child's collab rooms | **browsers** (`/_ws/collab/<slug>`, proxied) | studio process, in memory |

The only link between them is one-way and not live: the hub's
`afterStoreDocument` writes to disk and commits. Presence is ephemeral room
state and cannot cross a filesystem at all, and a browser edit reaches the
studio room and the disk but never the hub's document — so a desktop peer
subscribed to that document sees nothing. Two people on one project, one in the
app and one in a tab, never meet. That is the headline of the cloud product,
and it did not exist.

This is not an oversight. The hub was the sync brain first (Phase 9), the
browser-in-the-cloud surface reused the dev-server's own rooms (Phase 27), and
**DDR-209 / Phase 27 D2 deliberately forbids the studio child from syncing
out** — honouring the tenant's `linkedHub` inside a cell would dial OUT to a
third-party hub carrying their canvases, and start a SECOND autocommit over the
working tree the hub is already committing. The islands were left as islands on
purpose.

So the question this decides is not "should they be joined" but **"can they be
joined without reversing DDR-209"**.

## Decision

**Unify at the hub, by letting the cell pair with ITSELF.** The studio child
runs a `HocuspocusProvider` to its own cell hub over **loopback**, with
`MAUDE_SHARED_DOC` on, so the browser room's `Y.Doc` **is** the document that
syncs to the hub — the single-shared-doc model of DDR-064, which was fully
built and shipped OFF behind a flag out of caution, not because of a known bug.
The browser and the desktop then converge on one document by CRDT merge, and
presence crosses for free because the awareness bridged into the room is the
provider's.

DDR-209's two fears are preserved **literally**, as conditions rather than as
argument:

1. **No dial-out** — the hub URL must resolve to a loopback host
   (127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1). Anything else is refused. A cell talking to
   127.0.0.1 is a process talking to itself; nothing leaves the container.
2. **No second committer** — autocommit must be explicitly disabled
   (`MAUDE_SYNC_NO_AUTOCOMMIT=1`), and under pairing the autocommit object is
   never *constructed*, so there is no later branch that could reach a commit.
   The hub's `afterStoreDocument` remains the only committer.

A third condition is ours and narrows further: **shared-doc must be on**.
Without it the loopback provider would open a second `Y.Doc` per canvas beside
the room's — the two-doc world this exists to collapse — and its agent would
become a second doc→file writer for no benefit at all.

The tenant's `.design/config.json` supplies **exactly one** field: `workspaceId`.
Not the URL — that would be the dial-out. But the workspace id decides the wire
document name (DDR-192 §5), and the desktop resolves it from that same field; a
cell that derived a different one would put the browser and the desktop on two
differently-named documents and this whole feature would silently keep doing
what it did before.

### Why the credential is a minted store token and not `HUB_SECRET`

The studio child's environment is deliberately minimal so that a process
handling tenant-shaped requests does not hold the hub's admin bearer. Passing
`HUB_SECRET` to buy a Yjs connection would trade away the reason that minimal
environment exists. The hub mints a scope-`*` token into its own store at boot
(`INSERT OR REPLACE` by label, so the previous value dies rather than
accumulates) and the raw value exists only long enough to reach the child it is
about to spawn. It unlocks documents; it does not unlock `/internal/*` or the
admin API.

Scope `*` rather than a narrower binding because **a cell hub holds exactly one
tenant** — the container boundary already is the scope. Narrowing further would
mean guessing the wire namespace (which depends on the tenant's config and their
current branch) and silently failing to sync whenever the guess was wrong, which
is the failure being fixed.

### Rollout

`CELL_LIVE_PAIRING` is a **per-tenant allowlist**, default off, `*` spelled out
for the fleet. This changes the CRDT layer, so it rolls to one pilot project
(`alligators`), is watched, and only then widens. A fleet-wide boolean would
make the pilot step impossible to express. Env applies at container start, so
changing it needs a real stop → wake, not a config re-push.

## What this cost elsewhere

Four things surfaced while threading the needle, and each is part of the
decision rather than incidental:

- **`.claudeignore` is not written in a cell.** The untrusted-canvas markers
  exist for Claude Code reading the checkout, and nothing runs Claude against a
  cell's tree. `.claudeignore` lives at the repo root, so writing it would put a
  machine-authored file into the tenant's repository, which the hub would then
  commit and mirror to their GitHub. The canvases are no less untrusted; the
  audience for the marker is absent.
- **A projection write announces itself.** In a container the recursive
  `fs.watch` misses our atomic tmp+rename writes, so a peer's edit reached the
  doc and the disk and then stopped: no `fs:any`, no `canvas-hmr`, and the other
  person's canvas iframe stayed on the old render until they reloaded by hand.
  `createContainerWriteBridge` closes that for API writes and cannot close it
  here (it triggers off `activity:suppress`, which the projector never arms), so
  the projector emits the event itself — delayed by the bridge's own margin, so
  a watcher that *does* fire wins and the HMR broadcaster's per-file coalescing
  collapses the pair into one reload.
- **A projection write that changes nothing now costs nothing.** The `last*`
  guards compare against what the projector wrote, which is null on the first
  pass, so the cold-start `reconcile()` re-wrote every canvas with content
  identical to what was already there. Harmless while nobody was listening; the
  moment the write announced itself it became a spurious reload of every open
  canvas at boot.
- **`sync/limits.ts` exists.** The byte ceilings lived in `sync/codec.ts`, which
  imports `Y_TYPES` from `collab/persistence.ts`. The moment persistence needed
  a ceiling of its own that became an import cycle whose only symptom would have
  been a `const` read in its temporal dead zone — a crash whose stack points at
  neither file. Numbers depend on nothing, so they now live where nothing has to
  depend back.

## The DDR-064 pre-cutover checklist, closed

Shared-doc shipped OFF behind an unfinished checklist. Turning it on for cells
means closing it, so:

| Item | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| **A1** — gate `.html` bodies like `.tsx` | **Moot, recorded.** Since Phase 3.6 `.tsx` is the only canvas format; discovery admits `.html` for legacy compatibility and no real project has one. Left as a known residual rather than pretended away. |
| **A4** — detect slug collisions | **Closed.** `slugFor` flattens `/` to `-`, so `ui/a/b.tsx` and `ui/a-b.tsx` produce one slug. Two files on one document is not degradation, it is each writing the other's body over itself forever. **Both** are excluded, not one picked: refusing to sync two canvases is recoverable by renaming; overwriting one with the other is not. |
| **A6** — cap pinned rooms | **Closed.** A shared-doc canvas is a pinned room, deliberately immune to the last-browser-leaves drop — which is exactly why nothing else will ever reclaim it. Ceiling 500 (`MAUDE_MAX_PINNED_ROOMS`), far above the largest in-house project at 83, so it is a runaway guard rather than a product limit. |
| **A7** — one-time consent notice | **Closed.** A one-time warn whenever shared-doc engages against a hub. A cell is exempt **and that is the decision**: the operator turned pairing on per project, the hub is the cell's own loopback, nothing leaves the container — consent was given by configuration, and repeating it per canvas boot trains an operator to skip the line that matters. |
| **comments hub→disk lane** | **Closed.** The codec capped file→doc; this is the other direction, and until shared-doc it barely mattered because the room's doc was populated only by browsers on this machine. Now it is populated by the hub. Same ceilings, so a value that could never be imported can never be written either. The write is refused, not the sync — the doc keeps converging. |
| **`@hocuspocus/provider` advisories** | **Closed.** 4.3.0, current major; `bun audit` reports nothing against `@hocuspocus/*` or `yjs`. (Nine unrelated transitive findings exist in the ACP SDK and `dom-to-svg` chains — pre-existing, off the sync path.) |

## Alternatives rejected

- **C1 — re-home the browser's collab onto the hub's Hocuspocus directly** (the
  proxy stops forwarding `/_ws/collab`; the hub serves it). Cleaner: one doc, no
  bridge, no second process in the loop. Rejected **for now, not on the merits**
  — it requires re-homing the room's other lanes (comments, annotations,
  activity) onto the hub doc, which is a large structural change to make on the
  strength of a model that has never run in production. C2 is the reversible
  pilot that earns the right to do C1; the follow-up is noted, not abandoned.
- **B — the studio child dials its own external hub / the tenant's
  `linkedHub`.** This is the thing DDR-209 forbids, wearing a feature's clothes:
  dial-out plus a second autocommit. Off the table.
- **Let the hub remain the only doc→file writer and have the studio skip its
  projection.** Tempting, since the hub already writes on `afterStoreDocument`
  through a twin of the same merge (`meta-merge.mjs`, held byte-identical by
  test). Rejected because the ordering then stops being ours: the studio would
  have to announce a reload for a file another process had not necessarily
  written yet. Both writers producing identical bytes is redundant and cheap;
  the echo guard drops the second event and the HMR debounce collapses the pair.

## Consequences

- **Attribution changes for browser-originated edits.** They now reach the hub
  over the loopback connection, so `afterStoreDocument` attributes the commit to
  the pairing token rather than to the member. The token is minted with **no
  owner** deliberately — signing a tenant's git history with a machine identity
  dressed up as a person is worse than an honest "unknown". Carrying the real
  editor across the loopback lane is follow-up work, and it is the first thing
  C1 would fix for free.
- Beyond the cell, nothing moves: `MAUDE_SHARED_DOC` stays off by default for
  desktop and self-hosted hubs, and the guard is inert outside workspace mode.
- The live cross-surface run (two surfaces, cursors both ways, reload loses
  nothing, exactly one committer in `git log`) is the gate this decision is
  conditional on. Passing tests are the floor, not the proof.

## Context

Cloud Phase 27 put the real studio inside the cell, and a member opening
`<project>.cloud.maude.sh` now loads the byte-identical client the desktop
loads. What they do not get is the other person.

A cell holds **two disjoint `Y.Doc` worlds**:

| | who connects | where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the hub's Hocuspocus documents | the **desktop** (`linkedHub` → the cell) | hub process, SQLite-backed, durable |
| the studio child's collab rooms | **browsers** (`/_ws/collab/<slug>`, proxied) | studio process, in memory |

The only link between them is one-way and not live: the hub's
`afterStoreDocument` writes to disk and commits. Presence is ephemeral room
state and cannot cross a filesystem at all, and a browser edit reaches the
studio room and the disk but never the hub's document — so a desktop peer
subscribed to that document sees nothing. Two people on one project, one in the
app and one in a tab, never meet. That is the headline of the cloud product,
and it did not exist.

browser-in-the-cloud surface reused the dev-server's own rooms (Phase 27), and
**DDR-209 / Phase 27 D2 deliberately forbids the studio child from syncing
out** — honouring the tenant's `linkedHub` inside a cell would dial OUT to a
third-party hub carrying their canvases, and start a SECOND autocommit over the
working tree the hub is already committing. The islands were left as islands on
purpose.

So the question this decides is not "should they be joined" but **"can they be
joined without reversing DDR-209"**.

## Decision

**Unify at the hub, by letting the cell pair with ITSELF.** The studio child
runs a `HocuspocusProvider` to its own cell hub over **loopback**, with
`MAUDE_SHARED_DOC` on, so the browser room's `Y.Doc` **is** the document that
syncs to the hub — the single-shared-doc model of DDR-064, which was fully
built and shipped OFF behind a flag out of caution, not because of a known bug.

presence crosses for free because the awareness bridged into the room is the
provider's.

argument:

1. **No dial-out** — the hub URL must resolve to a loopback host

   never *constructed*, so there is no later branch that could reach a commit.

the room's — the two-doc world this exists to collapse — and its agent would
become a second doc→file writer for no benefit at all.

The tenant's `.design/config.json` supplies **exactly one** field: `workspaceId`.

document name (DDR-192 §5), and the desktop resolves it from that same field; a

differently-named documents and this whole feature would silently keep doing
what it did before.

handling tenant-shaped requests does not hold the hub's admin bearer. Passing

accumulates) and the raw value exists only long enough to reach the child it is

admin API.

decision.rationale:
A cell's hub owns the tenant's history and commits every edit as it lands (the studio child's own autocommit is disabled so there is one committer). The shared studio client nonetheless rendered the full working-tree surface there — an 'unsaved changes' list, Save version, Publish, and a read-only hint telling a browser user to 'save and publish from your terminal', which is advice a cloud user cannot take. The list was also literally false: it described work that was already saved.

Decision: the client withdraws the working-tree HALF of the Changes panel wherever the server owns history, and keeps History, which is the part someone actually wants there. Driven by `cfg.cloud` — present exactly when the hub runs the workspace agent that owns history, so the UI follows a server-STATED fact rather than re-deriving one. A new `historyOnly` prop on GitPanel; panel title, dock tab and View-menu row all read 'History'.

Deliberately NOT applied to a hub-linked DESKTOP peer, though it syncs to the same cloud project: verified that such a peer does not self-commit (its tree stays dirty), so hiding the surface there would remove the only way to commit its local checkout. The condition is 'the server owns history', not 'the project is in the cloud'.

Known edge: a cell whose git failed to initialise reports no history either way; the browser could not act on it regardless, since the panel is read-only there.

Found while verifying DDR-213 pairing on a local cloud-faithful cell. The '7 unsaved' that prompted it was a real bug (the hub never committed paired edits) fixed in the same change; with that fixed the status chip reads 'all saved' on its own.

decision.title: Security review (defender): cell autocommit commit-set widening + annotations path
decision.rationale:
## Security defender audit — 6 files scanned (cell autocommit commit-set broadening + annotations path)

### Evidence sources
- Diff base: `512ab5a4` (branch `main`, uncommitted working tree)
- Config: no `security` block in `.ai/workflows.config.json` → `severityFloor = medium`, `scope` default (classic in scope)
- Changed files in scope: `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs`, `apps/hub/src/workspace-files.mjs`, `apps/hub/test/workspace-agent.test.mjs`, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/panels/GitPanel.jsx` (+ `apps/studio/dist/client.bundle.js` — generated, skipped)
- Also in the working tree, audited for surface: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.claude/settings.json`
- Lockfile changes: yes (see Dependency surface)
- Prior decisions read: DDR-213, DDR-209, DDR-115, DDR-064, DDR-054
- Two git behaviours below were verified empirically in a throwaway repo, not asserted from memory.

---

### Blockers (severity >= medium)

#### 1. `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs:232-239` — **A3 authz / trust-boundary control bypass** (high)

Snippet:
```js
.filter(([, inDoc, onDiskText]) => inDoc !== null && onDiskText !== null)
```

**Why.** The meta lane's *write* gate and its new *commit* gate disagree, and the commit gate is the looser one.
`filesForCanvas` only writes meta when `mergeSharedMetaIntoLocal(...) !== null`, and its own docblock states the contract:
"null means the doc's shared meta did not parse. Skipping is the only safe answer." `committable` gates on
`content.meta !== null` — true for *any* non-empty string, including one that is not JSON, not an object, or an array.
So when a peer puts a non-object string in the meta `Y.Text`, the hub writes nothing (correctly refusing) and then
stages and commits `<stem>.meta.json` **verbatim, unmerged, unvalidated, and un-authored by the hub**.

That is the one lane where committed bytes can differ from doc bytes. Body / css / annotations are safe by
construction: when the doc lane differs from disk, `put()` overwrites disk with the doc content *before* staging, so
committed == doc. Meta is the exception precisely because it has a validation gate — and the commit path routes
around it.

The sink is external. `scheduleMirror` (`apps/hub/src/cell-ops.mjs:197`) pushes the checkout to the customer's GitHub
on a clock — `backup` mode to a disjoint branch, `design-sync` mode as a PR into their working repo. And the disk
side is reachable from the untrusted principal: `PATCH /_api/canvas-meta` is in `CANVAS_SAFE_API`
(`apps/studio/http.ts:4671`), and `patchCanvasMeta`'s layout lane (`apps/studio/api.ts:1757-1779`) writes
`next.layout = patch.layout` — an arbitrary JSON object, no schema, no size cap beyond `readJson`'s 256 KB — into the
versioned `.meta.json`, refused only for `projectReadOnly` sessions. So a DDR-054-untrusted canvas origin plants the
bytes and a peer's malformed meta lane makes the hub publish them.

Under DDR-209 the hub is the sole committer specifically so that one validated process decides what enters history.
This is that control being bypassed by the process that owns it.

**Fix.** Derive the meta entry of `committable` from the same decision the write path made — gate it on
`mergeSharedMetaIntoLocal(content.meta, onDisk.meta) !== null`, or simply drop meta from `committable` and let it be
staged only when it appears in `writes`. The other three lanes do not need this.

---

#### 2. `apps/studio/sync/autocommit.ts:242-246` (reached via the widened note-set) — **A12 error handling / silent history loss** (medium)

Snippet:
```js
const add = await run(['add', '--', ...files], { cwd: repoRoot });
if (add.code !== 0) { log.warn?.(...); return { ok: false, reason: 'git-failed', ... }; }
```

**Why.** Verified: `git add -- <missing untracked path>` exits **128**. On `add` failure `commitCycle` returns
without re-queuing `files` — unlike the `commit` failure branch three lines below, which does
(`for (const f of files) touched.add(f)`). So one bad pathspec silently drops the **entire coalesced batch**,
including other users' real edits, from history forever.

The diff materially widens the window. Previously every noted path had just been written by the hub, so it provably
existed. Now paths are noted on the strength of a `readIfPresent` taken up to `debounceMs` (default **3000 ms** — the
cell passes no override) before the `git add`, for files whose lifecycle the hub does not own (the studio child's
projector, `collab/persistence.ts`, `DELETE /_api/canvas`). A canvas deleted inside the quiescence window now takes
an unrelated peer's commit down with it.

**Fix.** Re-queue on `add` failure exactly as the `commit` branch does, and/or filter `files` through an
`existsSync` immediately before staging (accepting that a tracked-and-deleted path should still stage as a deletion).

---

#### 3. `apps/studio/sync/autocommit.ts:250-271` (reached via the widened note-set) — **A12 error handling / autocommit wedge** (medium)

**Why.** Verified: with any unrelated entry already staged in the index, `git diff --cached --name-only` is non-empty,
so `commitCycle` proceeds past its short-circuit — and `git commit --only -- <paths with no changes>` exits **1**
("no changes added to commit"). That returns `git-failed`; `touched` is re-queued but **no timer is armed**, so
recovery waits on the next `note()` and then fails identically for as long as the stray index entry survives.
The tenant's history stops, and `/health` stays 200.

Before this diff, a batch consisting entirely of unchanged paths was structurally impossible — only written (therefore
changed) paths were noted. After it, that is the *normal* case: the comment correctly reasons that "an unchanged lane
costs one `git add` and produces no empty commit", which holds only while the index is otherwise clean. A stray staged
entry is plausible in a cell (a killed studio git verb under `MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT=1`, an ACP terminal `git add`).

**Fix.** Scope the emptiness probe to the batch — `git diff --cached --name-only -- ...files` — so the
`nothing-to-commit` short-circuit answers the question `commit --only` will actually be asked.

---

#### 4. `apps/hub/src/workspace-files.mjs:191` + `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs:246` — **A6 stored-content / missing sanitizer + byte cap** (medium)

**Why.** Every other doc→file writer in the system caps and (for annotations) sanitizes; the hub's does neither.
- `api.saveAnnotations` (`apps/studio/api.ts:1809-1831`) applies `sanitizeAnnotationSvg` and a 1 MB ceiling, with an
  explicit comment that the sanitizer exists "so 'inert' stays true for any future raw-render consumer and for the
  synced file a peer/Claude-context ingests".
- `collab/persistence.ts:166-173` gates through `withinByteCap(..., MAX_ANNOTATIONS_BYTES)`.
- `sync/projection.ts` gates html/css/meta through the same `limits.ts` ceilings (DDR-054 §2d).
- The hub takes the raw `Y.Map.get('svg')` string and `atomicWrite`s it. No sanitizer, no cap, on **any** of the four
  lanes (`MAX_HTML_BYTES` 4 MB, `MAX_CSS_BYTES` 4 MB, `MAX_META_BYTES` / `MAX_ANNOTATIONS_BYTES` 1 MB all unenforced).

The `siblingPaths` change is what makes this land somewhere that matters. For a **nested** canvas the hub previously
wrote `ui/Card.annotations.svg` — a junk path nobody reads (which is exactly the bug the change fixes). It now writes
`ui-card.annotations.svg`, the file `GET /_api/annotations`, the studio renderer, `read-annotations.mjs` and
`annotate.mjs` all actually read. So unsanitized, uncapped, peer-supplied SVG reaches the live consumers for the
nested case for the first time. (Flat canvases were already in this state — the two derivations coincide there.)

The XSS chain stays latent (`svgToStrokes` parses inertly, and `annotations-model.ts:1330` already treats a peer's
sidecar as untrusted foreign input), so this is medium, not high. The uncapped write is also the honest DoS answer
for Q4: a peer can push an arbitrarily large body/css/annotations lane straight through the hub onto disk, into a git
object, and out to the mirror, past ceilings every other writer respects.

**Fix.** Port `withinByteCap` (or a plain byte-length check against the same `limits.ts` constants — they are numbers
with no imports, so the hub's no-studio-source constraint is not a problem) into `filesForCanvas`, and route the
annotations lane through a sanitizer before `atomicWrite`.

---

### Warnings (below floor)

- `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs:199` — **low** — the containment check is **lexical**: `resolve()` does not
  resolve symlinks, and `atomicWrite`'s `mkdirSync(dirname, { recursive: true })` would follow a symlinked
  intermediate directory out of the design root. Currently unreachable — `listFiles` skips symlinks (`Dirent`
  `isDirectory()`/`isFile()` are lstat-based, so a symlink is neither) and `defaultBodyPath` is always flat — but the
  diff pushes three more derived paths through this check, so the margin is worth knowing about. A `realpathSync`
  containment assert would close it permanently.
- `apps/hub/src/workspace-files.mjs:53-62` — **low** — `canvasSlug` can return the empty string. `DOCUMENT_NAME_REGEX`
  (`/^[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]{1,256}$/`) permits `ws/a/main/..`, which yields body `...tsx` and an annotations lane of
  `<designRoot>/.annotations.svg` — a hidden file at the design root, shared by every dot-only slug. Contained, no
  traversal, but it is a junk write and a small cross-document collision.
- `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs:241` — **low** — every store event now arms the debounce timer, because
  `committable` is non-empty whenever body+meta merely exist on disk. Previously an event with nothing to write
  returned early. Under DDR-213 pairing that is per-keystroke-batch, and each firing takes the cross-process
  `maude-repo.lock` (`DEFAULT_WAIT_MS` 15 s) plus 2-3 git subprocesses, contending with the studio's browser git verbs
  which hold the same lock across network operations. No commit storm — the `nothing-to-commit` short-circuit is
  correct and the new test covers it — but the baseline lock and subprocess rate rose materially.
- `apps/studio/client/app.jsx:14098` / `apps/studio/client/panels/GitPanel.jsx:158` — **low** — `historyOnly` is
  presentation, not a control. Correct as written (the real gates are server-side `projectReadOnly` and the panel's
  own `readOnly={!isNativeApp() || viewerMode}`), but nothing should ever come to depend on it for authorization.
- `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs:87-92` — **low, pre-existing** — `atomicWrite`'s `.tmp-<pid>` sibling is left at
  the design root if the process dies mid-write. Never staged (never noted), so cosmetic only.

### Dependency surface
- New deps: 7 × `@1agh/maude-{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-arm64,linux-arm64-musl,linux-x64,linux-x64-musl,win32-x64}@0.55.0`
  added as `optionalDependencies`. First-party (own npm scope), **exact-pinned** (no range), sha512 integrity present,
  cpu/os/libc constrained, no install scripts declared in the lockfile entries.
- Flagged: none. No typosquat candidates, no `postinstall`, no abandoned packages.
- `.claude/settings.json` drops `vercel@claude-plugins-official` (surface reduction) and relocates the existing
  `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` env. `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` is pre-existing, untouched.

---

### Answers to the four threat questions

**Q1 — Can the broadened commit set escape the design root or reach a path the tenant did not author?**
No escape. The containment loop (`workspace-agent.mjs:198-204`) is computed over exactly the four values
`committable` later consumes — `bodyRel`, `sib.meta`, `sib.css`, `sib.annotations` — and runs before any read, write
or `note`. It still dominates every new path including the `canvasSlug`-derived annotations path. The slug is doubly
charset-constrained (`DOCUMENT_NAME_REGEX` at the hub door, `[^/]+` in `slugFromDocName`), so no separator and no
traversal component can survive; `..` degrades to the literal filename `...tsx`. `canvasSlug` removes separators and
strips leading dots, so it cannot introduce one. Every derived path is therefore either a real on-disk path from
`listFiles(designRoot)` or a single flat filename directly under the design root.

The `canvasSlug` collision is **not** exploitable for cross-canvas overwrite. `ui/Foo.tsx` and `ui-foo.tsx` already
collapse to one hub *document* (the doc namespace is built from the same lossy slug), and `indexCanvasPaths`
deterministically resolves the slug to exactly one body path. I diffed the three transforms —
`workspace-files.canvasSlug`, `api.fileSlug` → `canvasSlugFromRel`, and `sync/index.slugFor` — and they are the same
transform character-for-character, so the change makes the hub *agree* with `api.annotationsPath()` rather than
creating a collision. The residual attacker choice is "which `*.annotations.svg` at the design root", which is not an
escalation in a single-tenant cell (a peer can already open that canvas's own document) and can never collide with a
body, `.meta.json`, `.css`, or `config.json` because of the suffix.

**Q2 — Does staging lanes we did NOT write let a peer get arbitrary working-tree content into history / the mirror?**
For body, css and annotations: **no**. When the doc lane differs from disk, `put()` overwrites disk with the doc bytes
before anything is staged, so committed == doc; when they are identical the commit is a git no-op. For meta: **yes** —
finding #1. There is also a shared ~3 s TOCTOU window on all four lanes (disk read at store time, `git add` after
quiescence) which is inherent to any autocommit, but which now spans paths the hub never authored rather than paths it
had just written.

**Q3 — Can the meta lane leak or reset the `syncable: false` opt-out?**
**No reset.** `mergeSharedMetaIntoLocal` layers `META_LOCAL_KEYS` back from disk over the shared payload, nothing in
this diff writes meta, and `patchCanvasMeta` exposes only the `layout` lane — the canvas origin cannot set `syncable`.
**No steady-state leak either**, because staging an unchanged file produces no commit content; a `.meta.json` reaches
history only when it genuinely diverged from HEAD. The real exposure folds into finding #1: an untracked-or-diverged
`.meta.json` the hub never authored now enters history and the mirror, and in the unparseable-meta case it does so
with the merge gate bypassed. Note also that `syncable` is legitimately a versioned key, so committing it is not in
itself a violation — the problem is the *unvalidated* commit, not the key.

**Q4 — DoS: unbounded `git add` churn, commit storms, lock contention?**
No commit storm — the `nothing-to-commit` short-circuit is correct and the new regression test covers it. The real
availability items are findings #2 (a deletion race silently drops a whole batch of history), #3 (a stray index entry
wedges autocommit permanently and silently), the raised lock/subprocess baseline in the warnings, and the missing byte
caps in finding #4 (a peer can push an unbounded lane through the hub onto disk, into a git object, and out to the
tenant's GitHub).

### Notes
- The `siblingPaths` annotations fix is **correct** and closes a real bug: `api.ts:1797`, `sync/index.ts:1344` and
  `canvas-artifacts.ts:95` all key the sidecar by the flat slug at the design root, so the previous sibling derivation
  wrote and committed a path nobody read. The regression test asserts the right thing.
- The `historyOnly` client change is clean — no injection, no `innerHTML`, no user-controlled data. The `labels?.[id]`
  lookup is over an internally-constructed object with internal-constant keys.
- Prompt-injection surface worth passing to `ethical-hacker` (§B, not my lane): `read-annotations.mjs` and
  `annotate.mjs` feed `.annotations.svg` text into Claude context, and finding #4 removes the sanitizer from the
  writer that now populates that file for nested canvases.

Summary: 4 blockers, 5 warnings, 3 notes.
