decision.title: Security review (attacker): cell autocommit commit-set widening + annotations path
decision.rationale:
## Security attacker review — adversarial threat model

**Target:** uncommitted working-tree change on `main`, HEAD `512ab5a4`
**Date:** 2026-08-06
**Posture:** paid red-team pass. The defender's checklist is assumed done; nothing here is a re-file.

### Change summary
- Plan: no active plan (`.ai/state/STATE.md` → "done — desktop ↔ cloud live pairing closed 2026-08-06"); the change is post-DDR-213 follow-up.
- Diff base: working tree vs. `HEAD` (512ab5a4).
- Files in scope: `apps/hub/src/workspace-agent.mjs`, `apps/hub/src/workspace-files.mjs`, `apps/hub/test/workspace-agent.test.mjs`, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/panels/GitPanel.jsx`. (Also `.claude/settings.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `dist/client.bundle.js` — noted, not the subject.)
- AI / MCP surface touched: **yes, indirectly** — the change decides which bytes land in a file that `read-annotations` / `annotate` / `/design:new` ingest feed into a model context, and which bytes reach the tenant's GitHub mirror.

### Threat model — trust boundaries

| Boundary | What this diff changes about it |
| --- | --- |
| Y.Doc (semi-trusted, DDR-054) → cell checkout | Unchanged in the write direction. **Changed in the commit direction**: the hub no longer commits *what it wrote*, it commits *what is at four derived paths*. |
| Cell checkout → tenant's git history | Widened. The set of `git add`-ed paths went from "paths the hub materialised in this pass" to "every lane the doc carries that also exists on disk", including byte-identical no-ops. |
| Cell checkout → tenant's GitHub | Unchanged mechanically, but the input set feeding it widened by the row above. The mirror is an **unattended clock** (`cell-ops.mjs` `scheduleMirror` → `setInterval(tick)`), not a human action. |
| Studio child (writer) ↔ hub (committer) | New: the hub now takes the child's on-disk output on faith. The child runs the full studio API surface and answers untrusted-canvas-origin requests. |
| Untrusted canvas iframe → design root | Unchanged route-wise (`PUT /_api/annotations`, canvas-safe, accepts **any** `file`), but the file it writes is now the exact path the hub commits — for nested canvases it previously was not. |
| Hub slug space ↔ studio slug space | **New**: `canvasSlug()` was an index lookup key; it is now a *path constructor* on the write side. |
| Browser shell → git service | Unchanged server-side. Only the client rendering changed, and the diff's own comment reasons about safety from it. |

### Findings (attacker narrative)

---

#### A1 — Commit-debounce starvation: a **viewer** can freeze the tenant's entire git history, silently (**High**, new)

- **I would do:** hold the cell's autocommit timer open forever, so that *nothing anyone does in the project ever reaches `git log`*, for as long as I stay connected.
- **By:** the removed early return. Before this change, a store event that produced no writes returned `null` before ever touching `auto.note()`. Now:

  ```js
  if (writes.length === 0 && committable.length === 0) return null;   // rarely true
  ...
  for (const rel of toStage) auto.note(relative(repoDir, abs(rel)), who);
  ```

  `committable` is non-empty for *any* canvas whose body exists on disk and in the doc — i.e. essentially every live canvas. And `auto.note()` (`apps/studio/sync/autocommit.ts`) **restarts the quiescence timer on every call**:

  ```js
  if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = setTimeout(() => { ... flush() ... }, debounceMs);
  ```

  `debounceMs` is not passed by `server.mjs` → `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 3000`. Hocuspocus's own store debounce is ~2 s. So a doc that receives an update stream faster than 3 s produces an `afterStoreDocument` roughly every 2 s → `note()` every 2 s → **the 3 s timer never expires**. `flush()` then only runs on `stop()` (SIGTERM / migration) or a branch switch.

  The cheapest driver is the lane the lowest role holds. `studio-manifest.mjs`: `'/_comments': { safe: 'read', unsafe: 'comment' }`, and `role-matrix.mjs` gives `viewer: { comment: true }` — deliberately ("comment is the single write a viewer holds"). Each comment mutation → `onCommentsChanged` → `syncRoomFromComments` → Y.Array update → store → `note()`. The proxied studio routes are **not** rate-limited (`rate-store` covers the auth/admin lanes in `server.mjs`, not the studio proxy). Pre-change a comments-only store produced `writes.length === 0` and touched the timer not at all — this is exactly the property the change removed.
- **Resulting in:** total, silent suppression of the one thing DDR-209 says a cell owns on the tenant's behalf. There is no error, no `nothing-to-commit`, no log line — `commitCycle` simply never runs. `MAUDE_SYNC_NO_AUTOCOMMIT=1` means the studio child will not cover for it. On an OOM kill / SIGKILL (rather than a graceful SIGTERM) every edit since boot is gone from history. The mirror clock keeps pushing a `HEAD` that never advances, so the tenant's GitHub silently reports "nothing changed today".
- **Cite:** §A (availability / integrity of an audit-relevant record); §B5-adjacent (a low-trust principal steering a high-trust batching mechanism).
- **Mitigation:** cap the debounce — keep a `firstNotedAt` and force a flush when `now - firstNotedAt > maxDebounceMs` (mirror Hocuspocus's own `maxDebounce`); and/or only `note()` a lane when it is genuinely dirty (`inDoc !== onDiskText` for the byte lanes, `merged !== onDisk.meta` for meta), which restores the pre-change timer semantics without reintroducing the pairing bug.

---

#### A2 — The hub now `git add`s bytes it neither wrote nor validated in this pass (**High**, new — structural)

- **I would do:** decouple "the hub committed this canvas" from "these are the doc's bytes", so that a commit signed with a human's name carries content the hub never derived.
- **By:** `committable` filters on `inDoc !== null && onDiskText !== null` — *existence*, not *agreement*. Two consequences, one deterministic and one racy:

  **(a) Deterministic — the meta lane the hub deliberately refused to write is committed anyway.** `filesForCanvas()` skips the meta write when `mergeSharedMetaIntoLocal()` returns `null` (shared payload unparseable, or not a plain object). The doc's `meta` lane is a Y.Text any member holds. One character (`[`, or `nope`) is enough. `committable` does not consult the merge result, so the hub stages `<stem>.meta.json` and commits **whatever is on disk**, unmodified, while the code comment two functions away explains that refusing to write is the safe answer *precisely because* writing the wrong meta "would drop `syncable: false`, which is a security opt-out". The refusal is now decorative: the file is committed either way, just not by the sanitising path.

  **(b) Racy, and now the normal path.** The disk read (`readIfPresent`) and the `git add` are separated by ≥ `debounceMs`, unbounded under A1. Pre-change, every staged path had been `atomicWrite`n microseconds earlier with hub-computed bytes; the race existed but the *authored* bytes were the hub's. Post-change the whole point is that the hub wrote nothing — the bytes are the studio child's, and the child is the process that serves untrusted-canvas-origin writes. `commitCycle` then runs `git commit --only -- <files>`, which commits the state of exactly those paths as of staging, so anything that landed in the window rides along under the last-noted author.
- **Resulting in:** the cell's history stops being an attestation of the collaborative document and becomes an attestation of a directory listing. `git blame` on a design answers "who designed this" with a name that did not produce those bytes.
- **Cite:** §A (integrity / non-repudiation), §B5 (confused deputy — the hub commits on the child's say-so, and "say-so" is `existsSync`).
- **Mitigation:** stage a lane only when the hub can name the byte source — `writes` (it wrote them) **or** `inDoc === onDiskText` (it verified them equal to the doc). Never stage a lane whose write was refused. Re-read and compare immediately before `git add`, inside the repo lock.

---

#### A3 — `historyOnly` is asserted as a security property in a comment; the server disagrees (**Medium** standalone, **High** in Chain 3)

- **I would do:** do from a `fetch()` exactly what the UI now says cannot be done, on a cell where the surface that would have shown the damage was removed in the same commit.
- **By:** the new comment in `app.jsx` reasons: *"the browser could not act on it regardless, since this panel is read-only there."* `readOnly` is a React prop. `studio-manifest.mjs` says:

  ```js
  '/_api/git/commit':  { safe: null, unsafe: 'edit' },
  '/_api/git/discard': { safe: null, unsafe: 'edit' },
  '/_api/git/checkout':{ safe: null, unsafe: 'edit' },
  '/_api/git/pull':    { safe: null, unsafe: 'edit' },
  ```

  `edit` is held by **member**, not just owner, and none of these is in the `REFUSED` block that `pruneForWorkspace()` 404s. So any member's session can POST them through the proxy. `commit(body)` accepts a caller-supplied `files[]` validated only by `isContainedRepoPath(dir, f)` — *repo*-contained, not design-root-contained. `discard(body)` reverts the working tree.

  The change removes the only cloud surface that rendered working-tree state (the Changes tab, the "N unsaved" count, the `aria-label="Changes"`). History remains — so a rogue *commit* is visible after the fact, but a `discard` (which leaves no commit) and a mid-flight dirty tree are now invisible to every member including the owner.
- **Resulting in:** a member can destroy another member's uncommitted work, or author a second-committer commit, in a system whose whole design rests on "the hub is the sole committer" — and the tenant has no in-product view that would show it.
- **Cite:** §A (broken access control by UI assumption), §B10 (a privileged action gated on a client render flag).
- **Mitigation:** do not reason about authorisation in a client comment. If `commit`/`discard` are meant to be unreachable in a cell, put them in `studio-manifest.mjs`'s `REFUSED` block (they will then be pruned server-side) — and, separately, restore a read-only working-tree view so a dirty cell tree is observable.

---

#### A4 — `canvasSlug()` was promoted from index key to path constructor, and it has drifted from the twin that decides the real filename (**Medium**, new)

- **I would do:** make the hub commit a decoy sidecar while the file the studio actually reads stays untracked — i.e. reintroduce the exact bug this change was written to fix, on names I control.
- **By:** the new `siblingPaths()` derives `annotations` from the hub's `canvasSlug()`, and the docstring claims it "reproduc[es] the studio's transform exactly". It does not. The transform that decides the real on-disk path is `annotationsPath()` → `api.fileSlug()` → `canvasSlugFromRel()` (`apps/studio/canvas-slug.ts`), which **percent-decodes**:

  ```ts
  try { p = decodeURIComponent(p); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  ```

  The hub's `canvasSlug()` does not decode (and, unrelatedly, converts `\` → `/` where the studio does not). For a canvas path containing `%` — e.g. `a%2Fb.tsx`, which reaches the design root from the seeded clone (`MAUDE_SEED_REPO` is an `https://` git clone of the tenant's repo, so filenames are an external input) or from a `git pull` — the studio resolves slug `a-b` and the hub resolves `a%2fb`. Two different sidecars; the hub commits its one, the studio reads the other. Under the new `committable` rule, if both exist, the hub commits the decoy while the live sidecar stays untracked — which is *verbatim* the failure the change's own commentary calls out as "worse".

  Same drift on the body lane, and there it clobbers rather than decoys: `pathIndex.get('a-b')` resolves to `a/b.tsx`, so browser edits to `a%2Fb.tsx` (opened at studio slug `a-b`) are projected by the hub onto a **different canvas's file**. That half is pre-existing; A4 is that the change made the same lossy function decide a filename.

  The parity test added in this diff does not catch it — `workspace-agent.test.mjs` models the studio with a hand-copied `slugFor()` (which also does not decode), not with `canvasSlugFromRel()` (which does), and the corpus is `['Foo.tsx','ui/Foo.tsx','UI/Deep/Bar Baz.tsx','a.html','.hidden/x.tsx']` — no `%`, no `\`. The test asserts parity against the wrong twin for the new use.
- **Resulting in:** silent divergence between what the tenant sees and what their history/mirror records, on attacker-influenceable filenames.
- **Cite:** §A (path handling / normalisation divergence between duplicated implementations).
- **Mitigation:** make the hub's `canvasSlug()` a literal port of `canvasSlugFromRel()` (including the decode), and change the parity test to import `canvasSlugFromRel` — the real function — with a corpus that includes `%2F`, `%2E`, backslashes and mixed case. This is the same "twin must be provably identical" discipline `meta-merge.mjs` already documents and tests correctly.

---

#### A5 — The hub's annotations write is unsanitised and uncapped, and now lands on the path everything actually reads (**Medium** standalone; **High** as Chain 2)

- **I would do:** put content of my choosing into a file that the tenant's own agent tooling parses and that gets pushed to their GitHub, without going through the sanitiser that was written to stop exactly this.
- **By:** two writers, one file, one sanitiser.
  - Studio path: `saveAnnotations()` runs `sanitizeAnnotationSvg()` (element allowlist, `on*`/`style`/`href` denylist, `script`/`style`/`foreignObject`/`title`/`desc` **content** removal) and caps at 1 MB. `collab/persistence.ts` routes doc→file through the same function.
  - Hub path: `filesForCanvas()` → `put(sib.annotations, content.annotations, …)` → `atomicWrite()`. **No sanitiser. No byte cap.** `readDocContent()` takes `doc.getMap('annotations').get('svg')` verbatim.

  So writing the doc's `annotations` Y.Map directly over the collab WS bypasses the sanitiser entirely and the hub materialises the raw string. That much is pre-existing — but pre-change, for a *nested* canvas the hub wrote it to `ui/Card.annotations.svg`, a path the change itself describes as "a file NOBODY READS". This change repoints the hub's unsanitised writer at `ui-card.annotations.svg` — the exact path `GET /_api/annotations` serves, `annotations-layer.tsx` renders, `maude design read-annotations` parses, `annotate` mutates, and `canvas-rects` consumes.
- **Resulting in:** the sanitiser becomes an optional route rather than a chokepoint, for the canvas shapes it previously still covered by accident. Plus an unbounded write primitive into the tenant's repo (no cap on any of the four lanes on the hub side, where the studio caps all of them).
- **Cite:** §B2 (insecure output handling — content crossing into a rendering/parsing consumer without the gate its consumers assume), §B1 (the parsed text reaches a model context — see the AI section).
- **Mitigation:** port `sanitizeAnnotationSvg` (or a plain-JS twin, tested for byte-equality like `meta-merge.mjs`) into the hub's projection, and apply `MAX_ANNOTATIONS_BYTES` / `MAX_HTML_BYTES` / `MAX_CSS_BYTES` / `MAX_META_BYTES` on the hub side. A cell should not be the one writer in the system that skips both.

---

#### A6 — `canvasSlug()` can return the empty string; the annotations sidecar becomes a dotfile shared by every all-dots slug (**Low**)

- **I would do:** open a doc named `ws/<ws>/<branch>/..`.
- **By:** `DOC_NAME`'s slug group is `([^/]+)` — `..`, `.`, `...` all parse. `defaultBodyPath('..')` → `'...tsx'`; `canvasSlug('...tsx')` strips the extension → `'..'` → strips leading dots → `''`. `sib.annotations` becomes `.annotations.svg` — a hidden file at the design root, which passes the containment check and which **every** all-dots slug collapses onto. Not a traversal (all `/` and `\` are dashed before the dot strip, and the `resolve()` containment check is intact) — a namespace collision plus a hidden file the tenant will never look at.
- **Cite:** §A (input validation on a derived path).
- **Mitigation:** treat an empty `canvasSlug()` result as unprojectable and `return null`, the same way `slugFromDocName()` already refuses a name it cannot parse ("guessing writes a tenant's work to the wrong file").

---

#### A7 — Attribution and commit-message truthfulness regressed with the wider stage set (**Medium**)

- **I would do:** get my edit into a commit authored by somebody else, and make the tenant's history describe canvases that did not change.
- **By:** `note()` is last-writer-wins for the author across the whole coalesced batch, and the batch is now much larger: every store event contributes up to four paths regardless of change, and (under A1) batches accumulate without bound. `commitMessage(files, who)` enumerates every path in `touched`, so `git log` reads `design: update 7 canvases` listing canvases with no diff in that commit. `CommitOutcome.files` — the value surfaces report — is likewise wrong.

  Under pairing the author for a loopback-originated store resolves through `attributionFor({ name: 'cell-loopback-sync' })` → the label fails the `u-[0-9a-f]{8,}` session-label test and no email is present, so history is signed `cell-loopback-sync <cell-loopback-sync@workspace.invalid>`. That is honest as far as it goes; the repudiation risk is not the machine label but the human one it displaces when a browser store lands last in a batch that also carries somebody else's lane.
- **Cite:** §A (non-repudiation / audit-record integrity).
- **Mitigation:** carry per-path attribution and commit the subset that belongs to one author, or at minimum build `commitMessage` from `git diff --cached --name-only` (what actually changed) rather than from the noted set.

---

### Exploit chains

#### Chain 1 — "Starve, accumulate, poison": total silent loss of a session's history (promoted **High**)

Composed from A1 (new) + a pre-existing fragility in `commitCycle` that A1 makes reliably reachable.

1. As a **viewer** (or any member), post a comment every ~2 s in any canvas — `/_comments`, unrate-limited through the proxy, `comment` capability, explicitly viewer-held.
2. Each mutation drives a doc update → `afterStoreDocument` → `note()` → the 3 s quiescence timer resets. No commit ever fires (A1).
3. `touched` grows across **every** canvas anyone edits, because one timer governs all of them.
4. Now poison the batch: `POST /_api/canvas` to create a canvas, let one store event note its untracked `<slug>.tsx`, then `DELETE /_api/canvas?file=…` (soft-delete moves it under `_trash/`).
5. Stop commenting. The timer finally fires. `flush()` does `touched.clear()` **before** `commitCycle`. `commitCycle` runs `git add -- …` over the accumulated list; the deleted, never-tracked path yields `fatal: pathspec … did not match any files`, exit ≠ 0.
6. `commitCycle`'s `add` failure branch returns `{ ok:false, reason:'git-failed' }` and — unlike the `commit` failure branch, which re-queues — **does not put the files back in `touched`**. The entire accumulated session is dropped from the queue, permanently.
7. Nothing surfaces it: the log line is `[autocommit] git add failed: …` inside the container; the browser panel that would have shown a dirty tree was removed in this same change (A3).

Impact: unbounded, attacker-timed, silent loss of the tenant's design history — from the role that is specified to hold no write power over the project. The mirror faithfully pushes the un-advanced `HEAD`.

#### Chain 2 — Untrusted annotation content → tenant's GitHub → tenant's own agent (promoted **High**)

Composed from A5 + A2 + the unattended mirror clock.

1. Get content into a canvas's `annotations` lane. Two doors: `PUT /_api/annotations` from the **untrusted canvas iframe origin** (canvas-safe by design, accepts *any* `file`, `annotate` capability borrowed from the viewing member — a confused deputy the code already documents: *"a hub-pushed canvas can write a sibling's `.annotations.svg`"*), or the collab WS annotations lane directly, which bypasses `sanitizeAnnotationSvg` entirely.
2. The hub materialises it **raw and uncapped** (A5) at `<slug>.annotations.svg` — post-change, the path everything actually reads, including for nested canvases where it previously wrote a decoy.
3. The hub stages and commits it without having authored or verified the bytes (A2), under whoever's name landed last in the batch (A7).
4. `scheduleMirror`'s `setInterval` pushes it. In `backup` mode that is a direct branch push to the tenant's GitHub; in `design-sync` mode it writes the `.design` tree into a folder of the tenant's **working** repo and opens a PR. No human gate on either.
5. The file is now read back by `maude design read-annotations` — whose header states its output is "structured JSON the `/design:new` ingest path folds into a generation brief" — and by `annotate`, and by any Claude Code session over the mirrored repo. Sticky/text strokes carry `text` verbatim into the brief.

Impact: an untrusted canvas obtains a durable, replicated, human-reviewed-nowhere write into the tenant's system of record and into their agents' context. This is the pattern the 2026 GitInject work names as the dominant failure mode — instruction-bearing files loaded from the same repository context the agent is working in — and the same shape as GitLost's public-issue → agent-context lane.

#### Chain 3 — Hidden UI as the control (promoted **High**)

Composed from A3 (new) + A2 (new).

1. A member POSTs `/_api/git/discard` with a victim's in-flight paths (`edit` capability, allowed by the manifest, not pruned). The working tree reverts to `HEAD`.
2. Within the same debounce window, the hub — which already noted those lanes as `committable` without writing them (A2) — runs `git add` over the reverted bytes. `git diff --cached` is empty for them → `nothing-to-commit`, so the victim's work is not merely uncommitted, it produces no record that anything was attempted.
3. The victim's browser shows the **History** panel (this change), which lists commits. There is no commit. There is no Changes tab, no "N unsaved", no dirty-tree view — removed in the same diff.
4. Alternatively the member POSTs `/_api/git/commit` with a hand-picked `files[]` (validated only as repo-contained, so *any* path in the checkout) and becomes a second committer in a system whose invariant is that the hub is the only one.

Impact: destructive, cross-member, and unobservable from the product. The one comment that would have made a reviewer check — "the browser could not act on it regardless" — is in the diff, and is false.

#### Chains explicitly ruled out
- No path traversal out of the design root: every `/` and `\` is dashed before the leading-dot strip, and the `resolve()`+`startsWith(designRoot + sep)` gate is intact and correctly placed before every write.
- No arbitrary *filename* in the tenant's repo from the annotations lane: the `.annotations.svg` suffix is structural, and the stem is bounded by the doc slug.
- **No viable chain across a `security-auditor` report for this HEAD — none exists** (`.ai/archive/logs/security-reviews/` has no `*-defender.md` for this change). The three chains above are composed from fresh attacker findings.
- **DDR-213's wildcard, non-expiring loopback pairing token is NOT re-reported** — it is an accepted residual. Assessed against this change: it is **materially worse by one degree**, not by kind. That token's holder could previously write docs that the hub would materialise and commit *as the hub's own derived bytes*; it can now additionally cause the hub to commit **disk bytes the token holder never had to put in the doc at all** (A2). The token's blast radius grew from "what I can say" to "what anything in this container has written".

### AI / MCP attack surface

`security.includeAi` is unset in `.ai/workflows.config.json` → default `true`. Section is in scope.

- **Tool surface:** no MCP server added, no tool description changed, no `plugins/*/` tool definition touched in this diff.
- **Model output → downstream:** not touched. No model output flows into a shell, SQL, path or HTTP body in this change.
- **Tool output → model input:** **yes, and it is the load-bearing one.** `<slug>.annotations.svg` is read by `maude design read-annotations` (own header: output is "structured JSON the `/design:new` ingest path folds into a generation brief"), by `annotate`, and by `canvas-rects`. Sticky and text strokes carry attacker-authored `text` into that brief verbatim. This change repoints the hub's **unsanitised, uncapped** writer at that exact file (A5) and makes it committed and mirrored (A2), so the injection is durable and replicated rather than transient on one cell's disk. `annotate.mjs` already sanitises on read for its own parse — `read-annotations.mjs` does not sanitise, it just declines to DOM-parse; regex-extracted `text` reaches the brief whatever it says. **LLM01.**
- **Trifecta check: FAIL — all three capabilities are in one loop.**
  - (a) *Private data:* the tenant's checkout, their `.design` tree, their GitHub mirror configuration; a control-plane-minted repo-scoped push token in the cell's `git push` argv.
  - (b) *Untrusted content:* the annotations lane (untrusted canvas origin, DDR-054; the collab WS lane bypassing the sanitiser; filenames and file content arriving via `MAUDE_SEED_REPO`'s `https://` clone).
  - (c) *Outbound channel:* `scheduleMirror`'s `setInterval` — an **unattended clock**, no human gate, pushing to the tenant's real GitHub (branch push) or opening a PR into their working repo (`design-sync`).
  The mitigation is architectural, not textual: sanitise at the hub write (A5), and gate the mirror on something other than a timer for content that no member authored through a sanitising route.
- **Confused-deputy paths:** two. (1) The untrusted canvas iframe borrows the *viewing member's* `annotate` capability to write any canvas's sidecar — pre-existing and documented in `api.ts`, but this change is what connects it to the committed, mirrored path. (2) **New:** the hub commits on the studio child's say-so, where "say-so" is nothing but the existence of a file at a path the hub derived (A2). §B5 both times.
- **Excessive-agency tools:** none added. Worth naming: `/_api/git/discard` and `/_api/git/commit` are destructive, member-level, and have no per-action confirmation server-side (A3) — the confirmation was the button this change deleted.
- **MCP supply chain:** N/A for the hub/studio diff. Note out of band: `.claude/settings.json` in this same working tree drops `vercel@claude-plugins-official` and turns on `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`. Neither is a finding; flagging that plugin-set changes ride in the same commit as cell security logic is a review-hygiene risk (a reviewer reading the hub diff will not look at them).
- **Output handling:** the hub writes SVG to disk with no sanitiser (A5). Consumers currently parse it inertly (`svgToStrokes`, regex readers), so stored-XSS stays **latent** — but "latent" was `api.ts`'s justification for sanitising on write anyway, and this change removes that gate for the hub-written copy on the path that matters.
- **Secret leakage via context:** none introduced. `mirror-push.mjs`'s discipline (token in argv only, never in `.git/config`, never logged) is intact and untouched.
- **Jailbreak resilience for safety-critical decisions:** N/A — no model gates any decision in this change. The nearest analogue is A3, where a *client render flag* gates one, which is the same category of error.

### Adversarial-creativity finding

**The quiescence timer became an attacker-held lock, and the lowest role in the product holds the key.**

Nobody reviews a debounce for authorisation. The change reads as "we now also note lanes we did not write" — a widening of *what* gets committed. The interesting consequence is a widening of *when*: `note()` is not just a queue-append, it is a `clearTimeout`. Moving the early return from "we wrote nothing" to "we wrote nothing and there is nothing to stage" means the ~always-true branch now resets the timer, and a comment — the one write `role-matrix.mjs` deliberately grants a viewer, with its own row and its own test because it is "exactly where a scope bug turns 'may leave a note' into 'may edit the project'" — is enough to drive it. The scope bug that row was watching for did not appear in the role matrix. It appeared in a `setTimeout` in a different app, three hops downstream, and it converts "may leave a note" into "may prevent the project from ever being saved".

Second, smaller one worth the same look: `flush()` clears `touched` before `commitCycle`, and only the `commit` failure re-queues — the `add` failure does not. That asymmetry is invisible while batches are small and same-tick. A1 makes batches large and long-lived, which is what turns it from a theoretical drop into Chain 1's payload.

### Recommended follow-ups

1. **Bound the debounce.** Add a `maxDebounceMs` (first-note deadline) to `createAutoCommit`, and/or only `note()` genuinely-dirty lanes. Test: N no-op stores at `debounceMs/2` intervals must still produce a commit. *(A1, Chain 1 — blocker.)*
2. **Stage only bytes the hub can account for.** `writes` ∪ `{ lanes where inDoc === onDiskText }`. Never stage a lane whose write was refused (the meta case). Test: a doc with unparseable `meta` must not stage `.meta.json`. *(A2 — blocker.)*
3. **Make `add` failure non-destructive.** Re-queue `files` on `add.code !== 0`, exactly as the `commit` branch does, and surface the failure on a status route. *(Chain 1 — blocker.)*
4. **Port the sanitiser and the byte caps into the hub's projection.** Plain-JS twin of `sanitizeAnnotationSvg`, tested byte-equal against the real one over a corpus, in the style `meta-merge.mjs` already established. *(A5, Chain 2 — blocker.)*
5. **Fix the slug twin and the parity test.** Port `decodeURIComponent`; assert against `canvasSlugFromRel` (the function that decides the real path), not a hand-copied `slugFor`; corpus must include `%2F`, `%2E`, `\`, mixed case. *(A4 — blocker.)*
6. **Decide `/_api/git/commit` + `/_api/git/discard` in a cell, server-side.** Either move them into `studio-manifest.mjs`'s `REFUSED` block or raise them to `mirror` (owner). Delete the client-side safety claim from the `app.jsx` comment either way. *(A3, Chain 3 — blocker.)*
7. **Restore an observable working-tree state in the cloud shell.** History-only is the right *default*; a read-only "uncommitted in this cell" strip is what makes a rogue `discard` or a starved autocommit visible to the tenant. *(A3, A1.)*
8. **Refuse an empty derived slug** the way `slugFromDocName` refuses an unparseable name. *(A6 — below floor, cheap.)*
9. **Build the commit message from `git diff --cached --name-only`,** not from the noted set, so history stops naming canvases that did not change. *(A7.)*
10. **Gate the mirror clock on provenance** for lanes no member authored through a sanitising route — or at minimum log, per push, which commits it is replicating to the tenant's GitHub. *(Chain 2, trifecta (c).)*

### Sources consulted
- Hocuspocus store-hook + debounce semantics (`onStoreDocument` / `afterStoreDocument`, debounce & maxDebounce, flush-on-destroy) — <https://tiptap.dev/docs/hocuspocus/server/hooks>, <https://github.com/ueberdosis/hocuspocus/blob/main/packages/server/src/Hocuspocus.ts>. *Applies because this hub runs `@hocuspocus/server` 4.x and `afterStoreDocument`'s ~2 s cadence is what makes the 3 s `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS` starvable.*
- GitInject — prompt injection in AI-powered CI/CD, arXiv 2606.09935 — <https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09935v1>. *Applies because its named dominant failure mode (instruction-bearing files loaded from the same repository context the agent operates in) is exactly Chain 2's `.annotations.svg` → mirror → tenant's agent lane.*
- GitLost (Noma Security) — untrusted content → GitHub agent context → exfil — <https://noma.security/blog/gitlost-how-we-tricked-githubs-ai-agent-into-leaking-private-repos/>, <https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/07/gitlost-github-prompt-injection/>. *Applies as the closest published analogue of the trifecta shape here: untrusted content reaching a repo-scoped agent with an outbound channel.*
- Simon Willison's lethal-trifecta framing (private data + untrusted content + outbound channel in one loop) — used as the structural test in the AI section.

decision.rationale: The deferred manual acceptance criterion ran against a cloud-faithful local cell and found three real defects in a code-complete, test-green feature: the hub never committed paired edits (sole-committer passed vacuously with zero), the annotations sidecar was written to a path no reader uses (and committed, and mirrorable), and the browser offered Save/Publish for work already committed. A defender+attacker fan-out on the fix found three more — the commit path bypassing the meta write-gate, unbounded quiescence batching reachable by the viewer role via comments, and an unscoped no-op probe that could wedge autocommit permanently. All fixed with regression tests verified to fail without them. Lesson: an acceptance criterion parked because it needs real infrastructure is the only test that runs the real topology.

decision.title: ACP writes are project-scoped; ACP bridges outlive their socket; the desktop sidecar becomes a pool
decision.rationale:
Four structural changes, executed together from .ai/plans/feature-acp-write-path-scope.md. They ship as one because the last one is only correct in the presence of the others.

1. WHERE THE WRITE DECISION LIVES — MOVED, not widened. `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` are REMOVED from `MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts). A bare tool name on that list means the Claude CLI approves the call ITSELF and the bridge's `requestPermission` gate is never invoked, so a path condition cannot be expressed next to an allow-list entry at all — only by moving the decision. Auto-approval now happens inside `requestPermission` via the new module `apps/studio/acp/write-scope.ts` (`writeTargetsInsideProject`), which grants exactly DDR-184's no-prompt-per-edit outcome for every write resolving inside the session's project root, and routes every other write to the prompt that already existed (Milestone B). This SUPERSEDES the claim recorded in bridge.ts that 'auto-approving Edit/Write is the accepted residual: edits land in the served project and are reversible via the _history/ snapshot stack' — that was not merely incomplete, it was the wrong claim: nothing constrained the target path, so neither half held.

Measured adapter contract (claude-agent-acp@0.57.0, 2026-08-07) that shaped the design and disagrees with the ACP type declarations: `toolCall.locations[].path` is `input.file_path` VERBATIM (no normalization/absolutization), so the plan's locations-vs-rawInput cross-check is TAUTOLOGICAL for Write/Edit; `NotebookEdit` has no case in the adapter's tool mapper and emits NO locations at all, making the rawInput (`notebook_path`) fallback mandatory; and the permission request carries NO TOOL NAME — it rides only on the streamed `tool_call`'s `_meta.claudeCode.toolName`, which the bridge now harvests into a bounded map. Every failure of that channel fails closed to the prompt.

Rejected: sniffing `toolCall.kind === 'edit'` (shared with any future edit-shaped tool) or `title` (a display string). Rejected: falling back to `allow_always` when no `allow_once` is offered — the adapter turns `allow_always` into a session-wide `addRules` standing rule for the tool NAME, which would silently restore the unscoped Write grant from inside the code removing it.

2. HOW CONSENT IS EXPOSED for an out-of-project write. `allow_always` options are stripped SERVER-side before being offered, and `resolvePermission` validates against the same filtered set, so consent is per-call and a crafted frame cannot pin a stripped option. The prompt renders the REALPATH-RESOLVED absolute path and substitutes its own headline — the adapter builds `toolCall.title` from the model's string, so a write to `~/.zshenv` was headlined 'Write docs/../../../.zshenv'.

3. ACP BRIDGE LIFETIME — RE-KEYED from socket to chat (apps/studio/acp/index.ts). `bridges` was keyed by `ws.data.id` and `onClose` called `bridge.stop()` immediately, so any socket close killed the running agent; `RepoBranchSwitcher.jsx` reloads unconditionally at three call sites, so a branch switch silently destroyed in-flight work. Bridges are now keyed by CHAT and outlive their socket, with a grace TTL, a `MAX_DETACHED_BRIDGES` ceiling and least-recently-active eviction (detaching removed the natural reaper that socket-close used to be). The re-attach seam is the TRANSCRIPT LINE COUNT: every `update` frame carries its `seq`, `GET /_api/acp/chat` returns the marker as `X-Maude-Chat-Seq`, and a new `attach` frame replays exactly the gap — no duplicated tail, no hole. A permission request raised while detached still hits the existing timeout and fail-closed denies; 'no UI attached' must never read as consent.

4. DESKTOP SIDECAR — SINGLE CHILD BECOMES A POOL (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs). `switch_project` killed the child so the supervisor would respawn at the new root, tearing down the whole server process and every chat in the project being left. It is now spawn-or-attach over a `MAX_INSTANCES`-capped pool keyed by project root; the supervisor respawns the root that actually died rather than 'the current project'; `_server.json` is deleted ONLY on the spawn path (with a pool it may be a live instance's state, and deleting it would orphan a healthy server); the idle reaper asks each instance's own new `GET /_api/acp/running` endpoint; and `kill_server` drains the whole pool on quit. This is Options 1+2 of the plan's table. Option 3 (one long-lived cross-project agent host) was REJECTED: an agent process spanning projects would dissolve the per-project boundary decision 1 draws and reopen the scope question in the worst place. A pool keeps repoRoot — and therefore the write gate's scope root — one-to-one with a server.

Today a bridge's lifetime is one project's lifetime so the pin looks like ceremony; once decisions 3 and 4 let a session outlive a project switch, a gate re-reading 'the open project' would hand project A's session write access to project B. The pin ships with the lifetime change or not at all.

SCOPE NOT CLAIMED (recorded so no later document asserts a property the system lacks): `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` stay unscoped — this closes WRITE egress, not read. And `Bash(maude:*)` remains auto-approved and unscoped, so this does NOT establish 'an ACP session cannot write outside its project'. Named open items found by the Task-5 audit: (a) `maude design draw-build --script` ends in `exec bun run` and `to-lottie` runs an agent-authored python — an in-project write (now correctly auto-approved) followed by that verb is arbitrary code execution with zero prompts; (b) unscoped `--out`/`--out-dir` on eight helper verbs, of which `draw-build --out` writes agent-authored content to an arbitrary path; (c) `--root` re-targeting lets several helpers write under ANOTHER project's design root.

STATUS AT RECORDING: implementation complete and green (91 feature tests, full dev-server suite clean apart from one pre-existing flaky export-jobs test; biome/cargo check/clippy/import-coherence/version-parity all clean). The MANDATORY security-auditor + ethical-hacker fan-out this repo requires for every ACP-permission-surface change had NOT returned at recording time, and the desktop A→B→A switch plus the e2e scenario are verified by construction only, not by a live run.

decision.title: Cut the read-only Bash verb group from the ACP allow-list — prefix rules don't stop `>`
decision.rationale:
The nine read-only filesystem verbs — Bash(ls|cat|pwd|head|tail|wc|tree|file|stat:*) — are REMOVED from `MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts). `bashRules` is now exactly `['Bash(maude:*)']`. This SUPERSEDES the DDR-185 addendum's decision to admit that group.

WHY. Claude Code's `Bash(<cmd>:*)` prefix rule does NOT reject shell redirection, and every verb in the group accepts `>`. So `cat > ~/.zshenv <<'EOF' … EOF` matched `Bash(cat:*)`, was self-approved by the CLI, never reached the bridge's `requestPermission`, and wrote MODEL-AUTHORED ARBITRARY CONTENT to an ARBITRARY PATH in one command — with no write tool involved at all. Found and PoC'd live against claude 2.1.220 under `--permission-mode default` by the mandatory security-auditor fan-out (finding F1, HIGH). The group was therefore an unrestricted arbitrary-WRITE surface, not a read surface, and a cheaper delivery path for the DDR-054 / A2 chain than the write tools sitting beside it — which the sibling decision `acp-write-path-scope-and-session-lifetime` had just spent a whole feature scoping. That feature's write gate does not and cannot see a Bash call.

The prior justification (kept in the source, annotated) argued the group added no incremental READ capability because Read/Grep/Glob are already auto-approved and unscoped. That reasoning was CORRECT AND BESIDE THE POINT: it reasoned about the read surface and never asked what the shell does with the same grant. Recording this because the failure mode is a reasoning error, not an oversight — the next person to add a 'harmless, read-only' Bash verb will make it again.

CUT, NOT PATCHED — the same call DDR-185's own security addendum made for `find` (`-exec` is arbitrary command execution) and `Bash(agent-browser:*)` (a zero-click session-hijack primitive), and for the identical reason: a prefix rule cannot inspect what follows the command name, so there is nothing to patch. `pwd` is cut too; `pwd > file` redirects exactly like the rest, and 'but pwd is harmless' is the same beside-the-point argument.

ACCEPTED COST, deliberately: these verbs prompt again, giving back part of DDR-185's friction win. Judged the right trade — a write gate whose headline claim is defeated by `cat >` is worse than a prompt on `ls`. Read/Grep/Glob remain auto-approved, so the actual read workflow the group existed to smooth is untouched; what returns is a prompt on the CONVENIENCE INTERFACE to power already granted. Route them back, if the friction proves unacceptable, through a hardened `maude design` wrapper verb the way `agent-browser-safe` and `curl-local` already are (covered for free by `Bash(maude:*)`, zero Bash-surface widening) — a wrapper CAN reject redirection.

RESIDUAL, NAMED SO THIS DOES NOT READ AS EXHAUSTIVE (the exact mistake the F1 audit corrected): `Bash(maude:*)` has the SAME redirection property — `maude design slug foo > ~/.zshenv` matches the prefix. NOT cut, because `Bash(maude:*)` IS the design workflow (DDR-062) and removing it would put a prompt on every step of the thing DDR-184 exists to unblock — a materially larger decision than dropping nine convenience verbs. What redirection buys there is helper-CHOSEN stdout to an attacker-chosen path, weaker than model-authored content, but it compounds with the `exec bun run` of `draw-build` and the unscoped `--out` of eight helper verbs on the same rule. Open MEDIUM.

CONSEQUENTLY the write-scope feature's claim is bounded: the direct A2 delivery path is closed THROUGH THE WRITE TOOLS AND THIS GROUP, not in general. No document may state it more strongly while `Bash(maude:*)` carries those residuals.

Guarded by a dedicated test in `apps/studio/test/acp-session-allowed-tools.test.ts` asserting each of the nine is absent, carrying the PoC and its provenance, so re-adding one fails loudly instead of silently reopening the hole.

decision.title: ACP control frames are attachment-scoped — a socket may only address chats it is attached to
decision.rationale:
A `/_ws/acp` socket may act on a chat ONLY if it is attached to that chat. Enforced in one place — `entryForSocket` (apps/studio/acp/index.ts) — which every control frame now routes through: `cancel`, `permission-response`, `elicitation-response`, `set-mode`, `set-config`. `prompt`/`warm` deliberately do NOT, because opening a chat IS an attach and that is the feature.

WHY THIS NEEDS SAYING OUT LOUD. The property used to be free. Before bridges were re-keyed by chat (decision `acp-write-path-scope-and-session-lifetime`, Addendum Task 8), every control-frame lookup was `bridges.get(ws.data.id)` — the key WAS the socket, so a frame was structurally incapable of naming another socket's bridge. Re-keying moved the key into the FRAME (`{t:'cancel', chat}`), and the first cut resolved that `chat` against the whole `bridges` map. That silently widened the authorization boundary: any socket could cancel another chat's in-flight turn, flip its permission mode or model, or answer its pending permission request. Caught during the write-path-scope security fan-out; fixed by requiring membership in `wsChats` before the lookup resolves.

The practical exposure was low — `/_ws/acp` is main-origin + loopback only (never the untrusted canvas origin, DDR-054/DDR-123), and permission ids are `crypto.randomUUID` nonces only ever sent to attached sockets, so answering another chat's prompt required guessing a UUID. But 'you would have to guess a UUID' is a materially weaker guarantee than 'the frame cannot name that bridge at all', and DDR-125 F1's posture is explicitly the latter: a loopback frame must not be able to pin a value it was never offered. `set-mode` is the sharpest case — `bypassPermissions` is a real advertised mode, and flipping another chat into it would disable that chat's entire permission gate.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is why this is recorded separately rather than folded into the re-keying decision: re-keying a registry can silently DELETE an authorization property that was never written down because the old key structurally provided it. Any future change to what `bridges` is keyed by must re-establish this explicitly. Pinned by two tests in `acp-bridge-lifetime.test.ts` — a socket naming another socket's chat is a no-op (both bridges survive), and a socket naming its OWN chat still works (the client echoes `chat` on every response frame, so over-tightening would break the normal path).

decision.title: `_server.json`'s url is untrusted at every consumer — validate loopback at each, not just at navigate
decision.rationale:
`_server.json`'s `url` is UNTRUSTED INPUT at EVERY consumer, not just at the webview-navigate site, and each consumer must run it through `server_json::is_loopback_url` before use.

WHY THIS IS A STANDING RULE AND NOT A ONE-OFF FIX. The file lives under the served PROJECT root, which DDR-054 designates untrusted, and it is now WRITABLE BY THE AGENT WITHOUT A PROMPT: the write gate added in `acp-write-path-scope-and-session-lifetime` auto-approves in-project writes, and `_server.json` is in-project. So a prompt-injected session can choose its contents freely. `server_json.rs` already documented the field as untrusted and shipped `is_loopback_url` for it — citing an earlier security review F3 — yet the FIRST NEW consumer written after that (the sidecar pool's idle reaper, `has_running_chat` in sidecar.rs) passed the raw string straight into curl's argv, skipping a guard sitting 25 lines above it in the same file. The failure mode is that a validator attached to ONE call site reads as a property of the SYSTEM; it is not, and the second consumer inherits nothing.

WHAT IT BOUGHT AN ATTACKER (security-auditor A1, HIGH, blocking): `{"url":"http://attacker.tld"}` → an outbound beacon from the native app, entirely off the permission surface; `{"url":"-K/path/to/attacker.conf"}` → the leading `-` makes curl read the argument as `--config`, a form that can specify BOTH an arbitrary URL and an arbitrary output file, i.e. arbitrary outbound request plus arbitrary local write from the signed desktop process. Triggered whenever `reap_instances` probes that project — a background action the user never initiates.

THE RULE, in three parts, all now applied in `has_running_chat`:
  1. Parse to a `tauri::Url` and require `is_loopback_url` — the SAME predicate the navigate site uses. One rule, one place; do not hand-roll a second policy.
  2. Rebuild any derived URL from the PARSED value's `origin().ascii_serialization()`, never from the raw string and never from `Url`'s `Display`. Raw preserves a leading `-`; Display preserves whatever PATH the file supplied, so `http://localhost:4399/foo` would concatenate into `/foo_api/acp/running`, 404, and — because this particular probe reads a non-answer as 'busy' — quietly make that project un-evictable. Found while self-checking the fix for (1).
  3. When shelling out, pass `--` before the URL so no argv position can be reinterpreted as a flag even if validation is later weakened.
Failure of any check answers with the caller's SAFE default (here: 'evictable'), never with a fallback that proceeds using the untrusted value.

SCOPE. Current consumers are the webview navigate in `sidecar.rs::switch_project` (already guarded, DDR-109), `lib.rs`'s export-download URL resolution, and `has_running_chat`. Any new reader of `read_server_url` inherits this obligation. The pool (Task 10) multiplies the exposure: several `_server.json` files from several projects are now live at once, and one poisoned project's file is read by machinery acting on behalf of the whole app.

decision.title: RCA: cell live pairing never engages (env drift) + Open-in-Maude reports syncing that never starts
decision.rationale:
# RCA: live pairing never engages on the cell · and "Open in Maude" reports syncing that never starts

**Date:** 2026-08-07 · **Reporter:** 1aGh · **Investigator:** Claude (Opus 5)
**Source:** manual (tracker is `github`, but this arrived as a description, not an issue number)

## Summary

Two defects, unrelated in code and identical in shape: **a status that reports an
intention as if it were an outcome.**

**A.** `CELL_LIVE_PAIRING` is deployed, the Worker computes `MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING: "1"`
for `alligators`, the fleet runs `maude-cell:v0.56.0` — and live pairing is *not*
running. Two explicit `/_cell/restart` cycles (the runbook's sanctioned recompute)
did not change that. The release-guide's claim that `/_cell/restart` forces a fresh
`cellEnv` is, at minimum, incomplete.

**B.** After "Open in Maude" the desktop says *"Syncing with <project> — 68
canvases."* That sentence is emitted when the sync runtime has been **asked to
start** and the project **has** 68 syncable canvases. It is not evidence that a
socket opened, that the hub accepted the token, or that one byte moved. It is
rendered once, statically, and never corrected — so a lane that dies immediately
after start looks identical to one that works.

## A. Live pairing never engages

### Confirmed (measured, not inferred)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cell-loopback-sync` token in the cell's token store | **absent** (42 tokens, 0 matching) — queried via `/admin/api/tokens` with the derived operator bearer |
| `peersCount` after a clean restart, no tabs open | **0** |
| `CELL_LIVE_PAIRING` on the deployed Worker | **present**, `"alligators"` (Cloudflare API, not the repo) |
| Deployed Worker code | contains `...livePairingEnabled(env, tenantId) ? { MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING: "1" } : {}` |
| `livePairingEnabled()` logic | returns `true` for `alligators` (also with padding / different case) |
| Container application | `maude-cell:v0.56.0`, config version 34, `instances: 5` |

The token is the load-bearing signal: `mintLoopbackSyncToken` runs at **hub boot**
and is the first thing pairing does. `addToken` is `INSERT OR REPLACE` by label, so
a pre-existing token would not raise the count — but it would still be *in the
list*. It is not. Therefore `MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING` is not truthy in the hub process,
i.e. **the variable is not reaching the container**.

### Root cause (confirmed mechanism, one gap)

`@cloudflare/containers` applies `envVars` **only on an actual container start**:

```js
// dist/lib/container.js — startContainerIfNotRunning
if (this.startInFlight) return this.startInFlight;
if (this.container.running) {            // ← fast path, returns here
  ...
  return 0;
}
const startPromise = this.doStartContainer(waitOptions, options);
// ...
// doStartContainer, ~40 lines later, is the ONLY reader of options.envVars:
const envVars = options?.envVars ?? this.envVars;
if (envVars && Object.keys(envVars).length > 0) startConfig.env = envVars;
```

So `await this.start({ envVars: await cellEnv(...) })` in `cell-do.mjs` is, against a
running container, a **silent no-op for environment** — exactly what its own comment
says ("Idempotent when already running") without spelling out the consequence. Any
path where the container is up before the DO's `fetch()` calls `start()` keeps the
previous environment forever, and nothing anywhere reports the discrepancy.

**The gap:** `restart()` does `container.destroy()`, so the *next* request should
find `running === false` and start with fresh env. It did not — across two attempts,
the second with 75 s of settle time and a single wake request. The most probable
remaining explanation is that the container is being started by the **platform**
rather than by the DO (`instances: 5` for a single tenant suggests instances are
maintained independently of the DO's start call), which would mean the stored start
config — not `cellEnv` — decides the environment on every platform-initiated boot.

**This is not yet proven.** The decisive evidence is the hub's own stdout: it logs
`[hub] live pairing ON — minted…` or `could not mint…` at boot. Container stdout was
not reachable from here.

### Impact

- **Severity: high for the feature, zero for data.** Live pairing — the headline of
  the v0.56.0 cloud release — is dark in production for the one pilot tenant it was
  enabled for. Desktop and browser still persist to the same disk; nothing is lost,
  they just never meet live.
- **Wider blast radius than pairing:** *any* future change to `cellEnv` derivation
  is subject to the same silence. This already burned v0.54.0 (`HUB_PUBLIC_URL` /
  `frame-ancestors`), and the runbook's documented remedy is now known to be
  insufficient at least some of the time.
- No security impact: the failure is fail-closed (a feature stays off).

### Proposed fix

1. **Make it observable first.** Add pairing state to `/health` (e.g.
   `pairing: { enabled, tokenMinted, peerConnected }`). Today the only way to answer
   "is pairing on" from outside is to infer it from a token list via an operator
   credential. A feature gated per-tenant needs to say whether it is on.
2. **Close the env-drift class.** Have the DO compare a hash of the freshly computed
   `cellEnv` against the hash it last started with (persist in DO storage); on a
   mismatch, `destroy()` then start, rather than calling `start()` and trusting it.
   This is the "env-hash drift-restart" already noted as a follow-up in the release
   guide — this incident is the argument for doing it.
3. **Correct the runbook.** `/_cell/restart` is documented as *the* sanctioned
   recompute; this run shows it is not sufficient on its own. Record what actually
   works once (2) lands.

Files: `apps/cells/cell-do.mjs` (drift detection), `apps/hub/src/server.mjs`
(`/health` pairing block), `.ai/release-guide.md`.

### Testing requirements

- Unit: given a stored env hash ≠ freshly computed, the DO destroys before starting;
  given equal, it does not churn the container.
- Unit: `/health` reports `pairing.enabled` from `MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING` and
  `tokenMinted` from the token store.
- Live: after a deploy that changes a `cellEnv`-derived value, one wake shows the new
  value in `/health` without an operator credential.

**Complexity: Medium** (the DO change is small; proving it in the live topology is
the expensive half).

## B. "Open in Maude" claims syncing that may never happen

### Root cause

`apps/studio/sync/supervisor.ts:147` returns the claim:

```ts
await runtime.start();          // starting providers; does NOT await connect/auth
const canvases = runtime.size(); // how many are ELIGIBLE, not how many synced
if (canvases === 0) return { syncing: false, reason: 'nothing-syncable', … };
return { syncing: true, canvases };
```

`cloud/endpoints.ts` passes that straight through, and `CloudBar.jsx` renders it
**once**:

```js
setNote(connectOutcomeNote(r.json.project ?? projectId, r.json.sync));
// → "Syncing with alligators — 68 canvases."
```

`connectOutcomeNote`'s own hover text sends the user somewhere else for the truth
("Live status is in the 'hub sync' slot in the status bar") — an admission that the
modal is not showing it. Nothing re-renders that note when the WebSocket is refused,
the token is rejected, or the hub is unreachable, because `syncing: true` was never
a statement about the connection in the first place.

The irony is documented in the same file: `connectOutcomeNote`'s comment describes
replacing an earlier lie ("restart the studio server to start syncing") with an
outcome — but the value it now reports is still an intention.

### Impact

- **Severity: medium-high, UX/trust.** This is the first thing a new cloud user does.
  A silent failure here is indistinguishable from success, and the user's own report
  is exactly that ("vyskočí modal … ale reálně se nic nestane").
- Makes defect **A** invisible from the product side: a desktop attached to a cell
  with pairing dark would show the same cheerful sentence.

### Proposed fix

1. **Report the connection, not the attempt.** Let `boot()` await first-connect (or a
   short bounded window) and return a state machine — `connecting` → `synced` /
   `refused` / `unreachable` — instead of a boolean latched at start.
2. **Make the note live.** The status already flows: `_sync.json` + the `sync:status`
   bus feed the status bar. Subscribe the modal to the same source so it updates in
   place, and surface per-canvas progress (`n/68 synced`) rather than the eligible
   count.
3. **Verbose on demand** (the user's own suggestion): a disclosure in the modal
   showing the last N sync events — connect, auth, per-document join, rejections.
   The events exist; nothing renders them.
4. **Never render a terminal-sounding sentence for a non-terminal state.** "Syncing
   with X — 68 canvases" should be "Connecting…" until something confirms it.

Files: `apps/studio/sync/supervisor.ts`, `apps/studio/cloud/endpoints.ts`,
`apps/studio/client/panels/CloudBar.jsx` (+ the committed client bundle).

### Testing requirements

- Unit: a runtime whose provider is refused (401) yields `syncing: false` with a
  reason, not `syncing: true`.
- Unit: `connectOutcomeNote` renders a connecting state distinctly from a synced one.
- E2E (desktop): attach to a hub that refuses auth → the modal ends in a visible
  failure, not a "syncing" sentence.

**Complexity: Medium.**

## The pattern worth naming

Three defects in two days, one shape: **the code reported what it had asked for
rather than what happened.** The hub committed only what it wrote (so paired edits
silently left no history); the annotation PUT warned to a console nobody reads; the
attach modal reports the intent to sync. Where a status is user-visible, the check
should be "what observation would prove this false, and does the UI survive it?"

| `livePairingEnabled()` logic | returns `true` for `alligators` (also with padding / different case) |
| Container application | `maude-cell:v0.56.0`, config version 34, `instances: 5` |

The token is the load-bearing signal: `mintLoopbackSyncToken` runs at **hub boot**
and is the first thing pairing does. `addToken` is `INSERT OR REPLACE` by label, so
a pre-existing token would not raise the count — but it would still be *in the
list*. It is not. Therefore `MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING` is not truthy in the hub process,
i.e. **the variable is not reaching the container**.

### Root cause (confirmed mechanism, one gap)

`@cloudflare/containers` applies `envVars` **only on an actual container start**:

```js
// dist/lib/container.js — startContainerIfNotRunning
if (this.startInFlight) return this.startInFlight;
if (this.container.running) {            // ← fast path, returns here
  ...
  return 0;
}
const startPromise = this.doStartContainer(waitOptions, options);
// ...
// doStartContainer, ~40 lines later, is the ONLY reader of options.envVars:
const envVars = options?.envVars ?? this.envVars;
if (envVars && Object.keys(envVars).length > 0) startConfig.env = envVars;
```

So `await this.start({ envVars: await cellEnv(...) })` in `cell-do.mjs` is, against a
running container, a **silent no-op for environment** — exactly what its own comment
says ("Idempotent when already running") without spelling out the consequence. Any
path where the container is up before the DO's `fetch()` calls `start()` keeps the
previous environment forever, and nothing anywhere reports the discrepancy.

**The gap:** `restart()` does `container.destroy()`, so the *next* request should
find `running === false` and start with fresh env. It did not — across two attempts,
the second with 75 s of settle time and a single wake request. The most probable
remaining explanation is that the container is being started by the **platform**
rather than by the DO (`instances: 5` for a single tenant suggests instances are
maintained independently of the DO's start call), which would mean the stored start
config — not `cellEnv` — decides the environment on every platform-initiated boot.

**This is not yet proven.** The decisive evidence is the hub's own stdout: it logs
`[hub] live pairing ON — minted…` or `could not mint…` at boot. Container stdout was
not reachable from here.

### Impact

- **Severity: high for the feature, zero for data.** Live pairing — the headline of
  the v0.56.0 cloud release — is dark in production for the one pilot tenant it was
  enabled for. Desktop and browser still persist to the same disk; nothing is lost,
  they just never meet live.
- **Wider blast radius than pairing:** *any* future change to `cellEnv` derivation
  is subject to the same silence. This already burned v0.54.0 (`HUB_PUBLIC_URL` /
  `frame-ancestors`), and the runbook's documented remedy is now known to be
  insufficient at least some of the time.
- No security impact: the failure is fail-closed (a feature stays off).

### Proposed fix

1. **Make it observable first.** Add pairing state to `/health` (e.g.
   `pairing: { enabled, tokenMinted, peerConnected }`). Today the only way to answer
   "is pairing on" from outside is to infer it from a token list via an operator
   credential. A feature gated per-tenant needs to say whether it is on.
2. **Close the env-drift class.** Have the DO compare a hash of the freshly computed
   `cellEnv` against the hash it last started with (persist in DO storage); on a
   mismatch, `destroy()` then start, rather than calling `start()` and trusting it.
   This is the "env-hash drift-restart" already noted as a follow-up in the release
   guide — this incident is the argument for doing it.
3. **Correct the runbook.** `/_cell/restart` is documented as *the* sanctioned
   recompute; this run shows it is not sufficient on its own. Record what actually
   works once (2) lands.

Files: `apps/cells/cell-do.mjs` (drift detection), `apps/hub/src/server.mjs`
(`/health` pairing block), `.ai/release-guide.md`.

### Testing requirements

- Unit: given a stored env hash ≠ freshly computed, the DO destroys before starting;
  given equal, it does not churn the container.
- Unit: `/health` reports `pairing.enabled` from `MAUDE_CELL_PAIRING` and
  `tokenMinted` from the token store.
- Live: after a deploy that changes a `cellEnv`-derived value, one wake shows the new
  value in `/health` without an operator credential.

**Complexity: Medium** (the DO change is small; proving it in the live topology is
the expensive half).

## B. "Open in Maude" — sync mirrors the LOCAL file set, so cloud-only canvases never arrive

### The measurement that settles it

Taken live, desktop connected to `alligators.cloud.maude.sh`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop log / `_sync.json` | `72/72 synced`, `state: online`, 0 pending, **0 rejected** |
| Hub documents | **75** |
| Overlap (hub ∩ local) | **72** — exactly what the desktop synced |
| **Hub-only** | **3**: `ui-welcome` (2 931 B), `ui-how_to_use_maude` (36 532 B), `ui-how_to_make_video` (31 911 B) |
| Local-only | 8, all `_draw/*.proof` + `_photo-*` runtime state — correctly not synced |

The namespaces match perfectly, nothing is auth-rejected, and the sync is genuinely
healthy. **The three canvases that exist only in the cloud are real content, and the
desktop will never receive them.** That is the user's "nothing happens", made
measurable.

They cannot arrive by git either: the local clone's remote is
`github.com/1aGh/alligators`, it is 0 behind origin, and none of the three are
tracked there — so "Get latest" would also do nothing.

### Root cause

The sync runtime builds its provider set **exclusively from the local disk**:

```ts
const canvases = admitCanvases(scan.canvases, useSharedDoc);   // sync/index.ts:427
// scanCanvases() walks the local design root's canvas groups. There is NO
// hub-side document enumeration anywhere in the runtime.
```

One Yjs provider is opened per **local** canvas. A document that exists only on the
hub has no local file → no provider → it is never requested. Sync is a *mirror of
what this machine already has*, not a materialisation of the project.

For "Connect an existing local project to a hub" that is defensible. For **"Open in
Maude" from the cloud dashboard** it is the wrong model: the user's intent is "give
me this cloud project", and the flow silently delivers only the intersection with
whatever happened to be on disk.

### Why the modal makes it invisible

`supervisor.ts:147` returns `{ syncing: true, canvases }` where `canvases =
runtime.size()` — the count of **local** syncable canvases. `CloudBar.jsx` renders it
once, statically:

```js
setNote(connectOutcomeNote(r.json.project ?? projectId, r.json.sync));
// → "Syncing with alligators — 72 canvases."
```

So the sentence is *true and misleading at the same time*: 72 canvases really did
sync, but 72 is the size of the local set, while the project has 75. The number can
never reveal the gap because it is computed from the wrong universe. `connectOutcomeNote`'s
own hover text then sends the user elsewhere for live status — an admission the modal
isn't showing it.

(Secondary: after boot the hub shows **1** peer, not 72 — providers do not hold all
documents open. Expected, but it makes "72 synced" unverifiable from the hub side at
any later moment.)

### Original root-cause note (superseded by the measurement above, kept for the reasoning)

`apps/studio/sync/supervisor.ts:147` returns the claim:

```ts
await runtime.start();          // starting providers; does NOT await connect/auth
const canvases = runtime.size(); // how many are ELIGIBLE, not how many synced
if (canvases === 0) return { syncing: false, reason: 'nothing-syncable', … };
return { syncing: true, canvases };
```

`cloud/endpoints.ts` passes that straight through, and `CloudBar.jsx` renders it
**once**:

```js
setNote(connectOutcomeNote(r.json.project ?? projectId, r.json.sync));
// → "Syncing with alligators — 68 canvases."
```

`connectOutcomeNote`'s own hover text sends the user somewhere else for the truth
("Live status is in the 'hub sync' slot in the status bar") — an admission that the
modal is not showing it. Nothing re-renders that note when the WebSocket is refused,
the token is rejected, or the hub is unreachable, because `syncing: true` was never
a statement about the connection in the first place.

The irony is documented in the same file: `connectOutcomeNote`'s comment describes
replacing an earlier lie ("restart the studio server to start syncing") with an
outcome — but the value it now reports is still an intention.

### Impact

- **Severity: medium-high, UX/trust.** This is the first thing a new cloud user does.
  A silent failure here is indistinguishable from success, and the user's own report
  is exactly that ("vyskočí modal … ale reálně se nic nestane").
- Makes defect **A** invisible from the product side: a desktop attached to a cell
  with pairing dark would show the same cheerful sentence.

### Proposed fix

**The real one — pull what the project has, not what the disk has.** On attach,
enumerate the hub's documents and materialise the ones with no local counterpart.
The hub already exposes exactly this: `GET /admin/api/canvases` returns
`{ name, bytes, peers }` per document. It needs a non-admin, project-scoped
equivalent (the desktop holds a member token, not the operator bearer), then a
provider per remote-only doc whose first sync writes the file. Guard it with the
existing containment + `syncable` rules — a hub-named document must not be able to
write outside the design root (DDR-054).

Until that lands, "Open in Maude" on a project the user has never opened locally
delivers an empty-looking project, which is the worst case of this bug, not the
mildest.

**The reporting, which hid it:**

1. **Count the project, not the mirror.** Report `local ∩ hub`, `hub-only`, and
   `local-only` — a single "72 canvases" cannot express the gap that matters.
2. **Report the connection, not the attempt.** `boot()` should return a state
   machine — `connecting` → `synced` / `refused` / `unreachable` — rather than a
   boolean latched before the handshake.
3. **Make the note live.** `_sync.json` + the `sync:status` bus already feed the
   status bar; subscribe the modal to the same source instead of telling the user to
   look somewhere else.
4. **Verbose on demand** (the user's own suggestion): a disclosure listing the last N
   sync events — connect, auth, per-document join, rejections, and *documents skipped
   because they are not on this machine*. The events exist; nothing renders them.

Files: `apps/studio/sync/index.ts` (remote enumeration), `apps/hub/src/server.mjs`
(project-scoped document list), `apps/studio/sync/supervisor.ts`,
`apps/studio/cloud/endpoints.ts`, `apps/studio/client/panels/CloudBar.jsx`
(+ the committed client bundle).

### Testing requirements

- Unit: a runtime whose provider is refused (401) yields `syncing: false` with a
  reason, not `syncing: true`.
- Unit: `connectOutcomeNote` renders a connecting state distinctly from a synced one.
- E2E (desktop): attach to a hub that refuses auth → the modal ends in a visible
  failure, not a "syncing" sentence.

**Complexity: Medium.**

## The pattern worth naming

Three defects in two days, one shape: **the code reported what it had asked for
rather than what happened.** The hub committed only what it wrote (so paired edits
silently left no history); the annotation PUT warned to a console nobody reads; the
attach modal reports the intent to sync. Where a status is user-visible, the check
should be "what observation would prove this false, and does the UI survive it?"

decision.title: A peer may ask the hub what the project contains — GET /api/documents, scope-bound to its own sync token
decision.rationale:
Yjs has no enumeration, and the sync runtime opens one provider per canvas found on LOCAL disk. A document that exists only on the hub is therefore invisible to a peer by construction: a desktop carrying 72 of a project's 75 canvases syncs 72, reports "72/72 synced", and is accurate about the wrong universe. Reported as "Open in Maude does nothing" — three real canvases lived only in the cloud and could never arrive.

Decision: the hub gains a READ-ONLY document listing, GET /api/documents, returning names and byte sizes.

Authenticated by the SAME peer token the caller syncs with, never the admin bearer — a peer must not need operator credentials to ask what it is syncing, and the cell operator secret is derived from the platform master. Every name is filtered through the same matchesScope gate onAuthenticate applies per document, so a token that may not open a document may not learn that it exists; the route can never widen what its holder already sees over the wire. No document CONTENT crosses. A missing and an invalid token get the identical 401 so it cannot become a token-probing oracle. The hub-chosen name list is capped where it reaches the client (payload size would otherwise be hub-controlled).

DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED: materialising a hub-only document as a NEW local file. DDR-054 treats hub-pushed content as untrusted, and creating files is a wider grant than updating ones the user already chose to have. That is a trust-boundary change deserving its own decision and security review rather than riding along with a reporting fix. Consequence, accepted: after this change the missing canvases still do not arrive — but the gap is named instead of silent.

The consuming diff (apps/studio/sync/remote-docs.ts) compares WIRE document names, not raw slugs: comparing a namespaced hub against flat local names would report everything as missing on both sides, which is the doc-identity bug (DDR-192 §5) re-entering through the reporting path. An unreachable or older hub yields null and sync proceeds unchanged — making the listing load-bearing would trade a working feature for a nicer message.

decision.title: Cloud sync is complete and bidirectional — hub-only documents are pulled down, not just reported
decision.rationale:
SUPERSEDES the same-day decision that listed hub-only documents but deliberately declined to fetch them. That call was made on a DDR-054 reading — a hub creating NEW files on your disk is a wider grant than updating canvases you already chose to have — and the owner overruled it on product grounds: the listing is already behind a login, the caller is authenticated into a project someone granted them access to, and inside that grant there is nothing to filter. A partial project is not a project.

Sync now runs both ways in full. Local canvases go up as they always did; documents the hub has and this machine does not are materialised as real local files before providers are built, so they sync from the first boot. Verified live against a hub with two documents the project did not have: both arrived with real content (2539 B and 264 B, not stubs), the local-only canvas appeared on the hub, and the runtime reported 3/3.

WHAT IS KEPT, and why it is not filtering: (1) containment — a document NAME can never place a file outside the design root; that is the difference between writing your project and writing your filesystem. (2) The document name must match one of the two shapes a hub may legitimately use (flat slug, or ws/<workspace>/<branch>/<slug>), validated WHOLE. Taking the last segment of an arbitrary string accepted "../../etc/passwd" as "passwd" — contained, and still a file nobody asked for from a name that should have been refused. A regression test pins it. (3) The token scope gate on the listing, which is the access grant itself, not a filter over it.

Placement is FLAT under the design root, matching the hub own mirror-direction convention (workspace-files.mjs defaultBodyPath) and for the same reason: a slug is lossy, ui-card cannot be un-flattened into ui/Card.tsx without guessing, and a flat file is trivially moved while an invented directory tree is not. Moving it later does not break sync — both paths slug to the same document.

Degradation: an older hub without GET /api/documents, or an unreachable one, returns null and sync proceeds exactly as before. The listing is never load-bearing.
